item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — In case the Yankees weren’t dealing with enough injury headaches for a 6-foot-7 slugger, Spencer Jones was out of the lineup Saturday with a sore left foot/heel.
The rookie outfielder claimed it was “no big deal” and chalked it up to the wear and tear of playing on Chase Field’s turf Friday night after jamming his heel in Minnesota earlier this week.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
But after the Yankees just lost Aaron Judge to the injured list again with a right calf strain, the last thing they needed was Jones nursing an injury of his own.
“Just a little banged up,” Jones said before Saturday’s game against the Diamondbacks. “Playing on turf is different, hard on the feet.”
Aaron Boone also downplayed it, adding that he still almost kept Jones in the lineup before sitting him in favor of José Caballero, who started in center field for the second time this season.
“Just felt like especially being on the turf here, he kind of jammed that heel in Minnesota and being on the turf [Friday], so I think it’s just a day-to-day kind of thing,” Boone said. “I even view him as available tonight.”
Boone said he preferred to keep Cody Bellinger in left field instead of shifting him to center.
“I considered moving him to center, but Belli’s grinding too and the turf here kind of beats you up,” he said. “There’s some scenarios where I would move him to center. Tonight, just being on the turf and as much as he’s been through this year, I didn’t want to move him.”
When the Yankees officially placed Judge on the 10-day injured list Saturday, they opted for defensive versatility over offensive upside in his replacement.
That meant calling up Max Schuemann instead of Jasson Domínguez, giving the former another shot in the big leagues for at least a few days beginning this weekend against the Diamondbacks.
“Adding his versatility to our bench makes some sense,” Boone said. “And then obviously some different roster complications moving forward with the playoffs around the corner.”
Schuemann’s stay may be brief, with Jazz Chisholm Jr. potentially returning from the IL as soon as the upcoming series against the Rays at Yankee Stadium that begins Tuesday.
If Schuemann goes back to Triple-A to make room, he would not be available to be recalled for 10 days (unless he was replacing an injured player again), essentially ruling him out as an option for the AL wild-card series.
That may have played a part in Domínguez not getting the call this time, in case the Yankees wanted to use him as a pinch-running threat on their playoff roster.
The 23-year-old also offers value as a switch-hitter, but he has proven to be a defensive liability in the outfield.
The Yankees’ trip to Chase Field gave them a chance to reunite with former teammate Jonathan Loáisiga, who has finally stayed healthy for a full season in the Diamondbacks bullpen.
Shop Yankees Merch
The right-hander often flashed his talent during his eight-year tenure with the Yankees, but injuries too often got in the way.
This season, though, after signing a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks, Loáisiga has avoided the IL and pitched in a career-high 64 games with a 2.32 ERA entering Saturday.
“Been through a lot of battles over the years with Jonny,” Boone said. “It’ll be great to see him. Hopefully we can ding him a little bit here. I know he’s had a really strong year, which I’m excited about for him. He’s such a talented guy that for him, it’s always been about just being healthy. So the fact that he’s gone out there and had a largely healthy season, I’m not surprised at the success he’s had.”
The Diamondbacks held a 25th-anniversary celebration Saturday of their 2001 World Series team that beat the Yankees in seven games.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Aaron Judge, Yankees claim they know nothing about severity of superstar’s calf strain
item.dc:creator: Gary Phillips

Actually, both claimed that they don’t even know the answer to that question before the Bombers played the Diamondbacks. “I gotta talk to the trainers and figure that out,” Judge said when asked for the grade after officially going on the 10-day injured list. “They got all the reports on that.” Wait, the Yankees’
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — The Yankees continued to treat Aaron Judge’s calf strain like classified CIA intel on Saturday, as neither the back-to-back MVP nor Aaron Boone shared a grade for the injury.
Actually, both claimed that they don’t even know the answer to that question before the Bombers played the Diamondbacks.
“I gotta talk to the trainers and figure that out,” Judge said when asked for the grade after officially going on the 10-day injured list. “They got all the reports on that.”
Wait, the Yankees’ training staff hasn’t told Judge the grade of his strain?
“They haven’t told me yet,” said the captain, who is only seven games removed from a 99-day absence for a fractured rib that he approvingly skipped a rehab assignment for.
Okay, but surely the trainers told Boone, right?
Wrong, said the manager, as Boone stated that he hasn’t bothered to ask for the grade.
“It doesn’t matter what grade it is,” Boone said. “We’re at nine games left [in the season].
“If and when he’s able to be back, he will.”
It doesn’t matter? The Boston Sports Medicine & Research Institute begs to differ, stating a first-degree, or mild, calf strain comes with a 1-3-week timeline. A second-degree, or moderate, strain requires 3-6 weeks of rest and recovery before returning to full activity. A third-degree, or severe, strain “can take many weeks or months to fully heal.”
The severity of Judge’s injury is important because the second-place Yankees’ postseason will begin with the Wild Card round on Sept. 29 if the current standings hold. Judge is obviously instrumental to their chances of fulfilling their championship goals, but it is unclear if he’ll be back in time for the Wild Card round or any postseason action.
“I’d like to be back by the postseason. That’s definitely the plan,” said Judge, noting that the earliest he can return is the last game of the regular season. “So we’ll see. I got really no answers for you on any timeline or anything like that.”
Judge, who is continuing to throw, work out and get treatment, added that he’s “gonna do everything we can to get back as soon as we can.” Boone, meanwhile, said that he wouldn’t speculate on Judge’s timeline, but he’s “hoping for the best.”
“We’re gonna get him back or we’re not,” the skipper said. “That’s what we’re gonna work to do, and we’ll see.”
It is no surprise that the Yankees have not revealed many details since Judge hurt his calf in the first frame of Wednesday’s loss to the Twins, a game he did not exit until the sixth inning.
Judge has been notoriously withholding when talking about his various injuries over the years, and he prefers that the Yankees follow suit. They tend to oblige; Boone used the phrase “I don’t know” eight times while discussing Judge’s calf strain before Friday’s game.
The Yankees typically provide a grade within a day or two when a player suffers a strain.
One detail that Judge did share is that he strained the soleus muscle in his calf, as opposed to the gastrocnemius muscle. Judge’s understanding is that the soleus muscle is more “crucial” to running and hitting.
He also said that he “usually” deals with “calf stuff all year long,” but it doesn’t become public, and he doesn’t miss games.
It had been his hope that history would repeat itself, but a return to the injured list couldn’t be avoided this time around.
“I’m definitely frustrated,” said Judge, who has only played in 66 games this season. “I’ve dealt with strains before and kind of played through them, but this was kind of in a different spot where it made it a little bit more difficult.
“The focus is still the same: to get ready to go for October.”

item.title: [The Big Lead] Yankees make sudden change to lineup, remove breakout star
item.dc:creator: Lou Landers
item.description: The Yankees are already dealing with the loss of Aaron Judge, and now they have another outfielder on the MLB roster who is temporarily unavailable. Spencer Jones, one of New York’s biggest breakout stories over the past month, is out of Saturday’s lineup against the Arizona Diamondbacks with left foot soreness. The rookie told MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch that he expects it to be a one-day issue, which should provide some relief for a Yankees team that cannot afford another significant injury. Spencer
item.content:encoded:
The Yankees are already dealing with the loss of Aaron Judge, and now they have another outfielder on the MLB roster who is temporarily unavailable. Spencer Jones, one of New York’s biggest breakout stories over the past month, is out of Saturday’s lineup against the Arizona Diamondbacks with left foot soreness.
The rookie told MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch that he expects it to be a one-day issue, which should provide some relief for a Yankees team that cannot afford another significant injury.
Spencer Jones has become a key part of Yankees’ lineup
Jones’ emergence has been one of the more encouraging developments for New York this season. After struggling early in his rookie campaign, the 25-year-old has started to find his footing at the plate and has become the Yankees’ everyday center fielder.
Through his first 80 games, Jones is hitting .248/.318/.433 with 10 home runs and a 109 wRC+. More importantly, his September has been particularly impressive. He entered Saturday batting .340/.415/.532 with two homers, 12 RBIs and seven runs through his first 13 games of the month.
The Yankees have also been encouraged by the adjustments Jones has made against Major League pitching. Manager Aaron Boone previously compared his developmental path to Judge’s, noting that Jones’ enormous 6-foot-7 frame could become a major advantage as his adjustments continue to translate.
That makes Saturday’s lineup change particularly notable.
Yankees cannot afford another outfield injury
Jones is being held out as a precaution, with José Caballero taking over in center field Saturday. Jones has indicated that he expects to return Sunday, so there is currently no indication that the foot issue is expected to become a lengthy absence.
Still, the timing is less than ideal.
Judge officially returned to the injured list Saturday with a right calf strain and has no established timetable for his return. The Yankees recalled Max Schuemann to fill his roster spot, while the club is expected to rely more heavily on its remaining outfield options.
New York has already dealt with significant injuries across its roster this season. With the postseason approaching, the Yankees need Jones healthy and available because his recent production has given the lineup another legitimate offensive option.
For now, the hope is that Jones’ absence truly is nothing more than a one-day precaution.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees posted their starting lineup Saturday afternoon for the second game of a three-game set against the Arizona Diamondbacks, and Paul Goldschmidt was not in it.
New York is trying to take the series after a 9-2 win Friday night at Chase Field. Goldschmidt led off that game and finished with a hit, a walk and two runs scored.
The announced order put Ben Rice at designated hitter, Cody Bellinger in left field and Luis García Jr. at first base. Heliot Ramos started in right, George Lombard Jr. at shortstop, Austin Wells behind the plate, Anthony Volpe at second, Ryan McMahon at third and José Caballero in center. Cam Schlittler was listed as the starting pitcher.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Yankees 9/19 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF L. García Jr. 1B H. Ramos RF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B R. McMahon 3B J. Caballero CF C. Schlittler SP.”
Goldschmidt, a seven-time All-Star, is in his second season with the Yankees after signing a one-year deal in February. He entered Saturday hitting .253 with 85 hits, 18 home runs, 50 RBIs, 44 runs and one stolen base in 102 games.
The 39-year-old first baseman spent his first eight big-league seasons in Arizona. He made six straight All-Star teams from 2013 through 2018 while wearing a Diamondbacks uniform.
After leaving Phoenix, Goldschmidt spent six years with the St. Louis Cardinals and won National League Most Valuable Player honors in 2022.
The Yankees sit second in the American League East at 89-64 through 153 games. They have gone 8-2 in their last 10 and trail the Tampa Bay Rays by four games.
Arizona is third in the National League West at 80-74 after 154 games and 4-6 over its last 10.
Manager Aaron Boone has mixed Goldschmidt’s playing time throughout the second half as younger options such as Rice have taken on larger roles. Goldschmidt started Friday after sitting in recent games.
The veteran remains a respected presence in the clubhouse. The Yankees nominated him for the 2026 MLBPAA Heart and Hustle Award earlier this season.
Goldschmidt signed a one-year, $4 million contract with New York this past offseason after hitting .274 with 10 homers and 45 RBIs in 146 games during his first Yankees season.
He has 390 career home runs and 1,282 RBIs across 16 major-league seasons. Career numbers also include a .286 batting average and seven All-Star selections.
Saturday’s game was scheduled for late afternoon local time. A New York win would give the Yankees the series with one game left.
The Diamondbacks have struggled to find consistent production at first base this year after Goldschmidt left the organization years earlier.
New York continues to chase a postseason berth in the final weeks of the regular season. Goldschmidt’s availability as a pinch-hitter or late-inning option remains part of the roster mix even when he does not start.
The lineup change was posted hours before first pitch and immediately circulated among fans tracking the club’s late-season decisions.

item.dc:creator: Greg Joyce
item.description: PHOENIX — Without any guarantees of it happening, Aaron Judge is holding out hope of returning from a calf strain in time for the playoffs. “I’d like to be back by the postseason; that’s definitely the plan,” Judge said Saturday afternoon. “We’re going to do everything we can to get back as soon as we can.” Access the Yankees beat like never before Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees. That was a
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Without any guarantees of it happening, Aaron Judge is holding out hope of returning from a calf strain in time for the playoffs.
“I’d like to be back by the postseason; that’s definitely the plan,” Judge said Saturday afternoon. “We’re going to do everything we can to get back as soon as we can.”
Access the Yankees beat like never before
Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
That was a slightly less definitive statement than what Judge consistently said during the summer when he was trying to come back from a right rib stress fracture, which he did after three-plus months on Sept. 8.
But now the clock is ticking even louder, with Saturday marking 10 days away from Game 1 of the American League wild card series.
“Definitely frustrated,” said Judge, who played seven games after missing 84 on the IL with the rib injury. “Dealt with strains before and kind of played through them, but this was in a different spot where it made it a little bit more difficult.”
Judge did not reveal what grade the strain was, but said it involved his Soleus muscle, which he indicated was more important to running and hitting compared to the gastrocnemius muscle.
“The focus is still the same, to be ready to go for October,” Judge said.
In the meantime, the Yankees are banking on their summer without Judge paying off now that he is back on the IL.
“Lean on each other,” Cody Bellinger said. “The game itself is hard; if you add too much pressure on yourself, the game becomes even harder. So we really just have to play for each other, lean on each other, pass the baton, do your job and control what you can control.”
The Yankees did that on Friday night, racing out of the gates to score five runs in the first inning of a 9-2 win against the Diamondbacks, just hours after the team announced Judge was going on the 10-day injured list with a right calf strain.
But they also got off well at the beginning of June after Judge landed on the IL with a right rib stress fracture before their lineup became a black hole for an extended stretch during the summer. They had finally started to break out of it shortly before Judge got back on Sept. 8, but after having him back for seven games, they now find themselves in the same spot again, less than two weeks away from the start of the playoffs.
“We’ve played most of the year this way, and I feel like in a lot of cases, especially some of our key guys over the last few weeks have started to, especially offensively, get it going like we know they’re capable of,” manager Aaron Boone said.
During the 84-game span that Judge missed this summer, the Yankees ranked 26th in runs per game (4.06), 29th in batting average (.227), 27th in OPS (.681), and 29th in WRC+ (90).
But over the tail end of that stretch, and into Judge’s return, the Yankees started to hit more like they are capable of. That included the trade deadline addition of Luis García Jr., the emergence of rookie outfielder Spencer Jones, and Bellinger getting back on track after returning from his own hamstring injury in August.
Perhaps most importantly, it has coincided with the reemergence of Ben Rice. The lefty slugger was a game wrecker for the first two months of the season before Judge went down, then cooled off a bit during the summer (albeit with some good stretches along the way) before catching fire again over the last few weeks. Entering Saturday, over his last 22 games, Rice had hit .353 with a 1.037 OPS and five home runs, including his 39th of the season Friday night.
“Special year,” Gerrit Cole said. “Has made some really good adjustments from previous years, going into this year, and I think he’s really started to heat back up here the last few weeks after having to make some adjustments in the middle of the season. Not only is he really proficient with the bat, but he’s a smart player and a hard worker, which is leading him to have a really outstanding season for us.”
The Yankees need that to continue for however long Judge is out (and even if and when he returns) for them to play deep into October, though Rice isn’t looking at it as having to do any more — which got some hitters in trouble during the three-time AL MVP’s first absence.
“I would think that everyone just goes out there and stays within themselves, tries to put together quality at-bat after quality at-bat,” he said. “Pitching is always going to be doing their thing, like they have for us all year. So from an offensive standpoint, just do what we did [Friday]: go out and have a team at-bat, trust the guy behind you and keep the line moving.”
To Rice’s point, the Yankees have leaned on the strength of their pitching staff all season, but that was especially the case during Judge’s three months on the IL this summer, when they were able to scratch out enough wins in low-scoring games, with their pitchers keeping them in it almost every night.
New York Post may be compensated and/or receive an affiliate commission if you buy something through our links.
“We have a lot of confidence in here,” Cole said. “For the most part of the summer, we’ve been tested really, really hard and we responded, by and large, really, really well. We have a lot of perfectionists in here. We’re always striving to be perfect and trying to be the best. But the reality is we’ve had a lot of obstacles we’ve had to overcome and, by and large, we’ve played really well.”

item.dc:creator: Santiago Tovar
item.description: Returning to the mound after missing an entire regular season due to an elbow injury is a daunting task for any pitcher. That context helps explain why Gerrit Cole endured a slow start to his 2026 campaign upon returning to the New York Yankees‘ rotation. However, Cole’s recent surge on the bump has generated plenty of momentum within the organization. When asked whether the veteran righty would take the ball in the Wild Card round, manager Aaron Boone delivered a resolute answer: “I would expec
item.content:encoded:
Returning to the mound after missing an entire regular season due to an elbow injury is a daunting task for any pitcher. That context helps explain why Gerrit Cole endured a slow start to his 2026 campaign upon returning to the New York Yankees‘ rotation.
However, Cole’s recent surge on the bump has generated plenty of momentum within the organization. When asked whether the veteran righty would take the ball in the Wild Card round, manager Aaron Boone delivered a resolute answer: “I would expect Gerrit Cole to start, yes.”
Boone faces a compelling rotational dilemma, given the standout performances of his depth chart. Max Fried has anchored his share of gems, while breakout starter Cam Schlittler has delivered a dominant campaign, one that Boone firmly believes warrants American League Cy Young honors.
With Aaron Judge sidelined for the remainder of the regular season, the Yankees are relying heavily on their pitching depth to carry the load into October. That group could get another boost with Ryan Weathers tracking toward a postseason return.
Gerrit Cole #45 of the New York Yankees.
Cole’s rollercoaster season
Cole’s season started with immediate frustration before he ever threw an official pitch. Lingering elbow concerns during Spring Training delayed his season debut, forcing him to miss the opening two months of the championship schedule and putting extra stress on the Yankees‘ starting rotation.
Dominant, double-digit strikeout performances—including a 10-strikeout shutout performance over 6.2 innings against Kansas City and multi-hit gems against Chicago and Atlanta—showed he remains one of the most electric arms in baseball.
A recurring issue throughout Cole’s 2026 campaign has been his home run rate. When Cole misses over the plate, opposing hitters have made him pay, elevating his HR/9 rate above his career averages and making several of his outings much more high-stress than his strikeout numbers would indicate.

item.description: Aaron Judge regresará a la lista de lesionados, lo que significa que los Yankees deberán navegar el final de la temporada regular sin su capitán, y potencialmente parte de la postemporada. Jude fue inhabilitado oficialmente el sábado, en un movimiento retroactivo al jueves. El infielder/jardinero Max Schuemann fue ascendido desde Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre para ocupar el lugar del capitán en el roster. «La realidad es que hemos tenido que jugar gran parte de la temporada de este año sin él»,
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge regresará a la lista de lesionados, lo que significa que los Yankees deberán navegar el final de la temporada regular sin su capitán, y potencialmente parte de la postemporada.
Jude fue inhabilitado oficialmente el sábado, en un movimiento retroactivo al jueves. El infielder/jardinero Max Schuemann fue ascendido desde Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre para ocupar el lugar del capitán en el roster.
«La realidad es que hemos tenido que jugar gran parte de la temporada de este año sin él», dijo el manager Aaron Boone. «No se puede reemplazar a un jugador tan extraordinario como Aaron Judge, pero tenemos grandes expectativas. Esas no cambian ahora».
- Te puede interesar: Jonathan Loáisiga recibe a los Yankees desde el otro dogout
Judge se sometió a una resonancia magnética el jueves en Phoenix que reveló la distensión muscular. Boone dijo que no daría detalles sobre la gravedad de la lesión ni ofrecería una estimación de cuándo se espera que Judge regrese.
Al preguntársele si Judge volvería para los playoffs, Boone respondió: «No lo sé».
Prior to tonight’s game, the Yankees made the following roster moves:
• Recalled INF/OF Max Schuemann (#30) from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre.
• Placed OF Aaron Judge on the 10-day injured list (retroactive to 9/17) with a right calf strain.
— New York Yankees (@Yankees) September 19, 2026
«No tengo un plazo definido para su recuperación», dijo Boone. «No voy a hacer predicciones. Obviamente, le daremos tratamiento y veremos qué sucede».
Por lo general, incluso una distensión de grado 1 en la pantorrilla requiere de dos a tres semanas para sanar.
Judge piensa estar en playoffs
Como mínimo, el momento de la lesión implica que Judge estará inactivo no solo durante la serie de este fin de semana contra los D-backs, sino también en la serie de cuatro partidos contra los Rays la próxima semana en el Yankee Stadium. Los Yankees llegaron a la jornada del viernes a cinco juegos de distancia de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana.
El jugador de cuadro y jardinero Max Schuemann viaja a Phoenix y se unirá a los Yankees para el partido del sábado. Judge no estuvo disponible para hablar con los periodistas antes del inicio de la serie del viernes contra los Diamondbacks en el Chase Field.
«Es un tipo que quiere estar aquí todos los días», dijo Cody Bellinger sobre Judge. «Quiere estar en el campo y ayudarnos a ganar. Sin duda es una noticia frustrante, especialmente cuando trabajas tan duro y durante tanto tiempo para volver, y luego sucede algo así. Me siento frustrado por él. Ojalá sea algo leve y de rápida recuperación».
La fecha más próxima posible para el regreso de Judge sería el último partido de la temporada regular, el 27 de septiembre contra Baltimore. La Serie de Comodines de la Liga Americana está programada para comenzar el 29 de septiembre. En este momento, dicho escenario implicaría que los Yankees recibieran a los Red Sox en el Bronx.
«La ausencia de Judge duele. Todos sabemos que es el mejor bateador del juego», dijo Bellinger. «Para nosotros aquí dentro, la mentalidad es que tendremos que encontrar la manera de salir adelante. Creo que el talento en este vestuario habla por sí solo. Confío plenamente en que tenemos suficiente talento aquí para salir al campo, ganar y vencer a cualquiera».
Esa tarea será más difícil sin Judge, quien fue sustituido por un bateador emergente en la sexta entrada durante la derrota de los Yankees por 5-4 en 13 entradas ante los Twins, ocurrida el miércoles en el Target Field.
Judge comentó que sintió rigidez en la parte inferior de la pierna derecha durante la primera entrada.
«Intenté restarle importancia y ver cuánto tiempo podía aguantar, porque estos partidos son importantes en la recta final de la temporada», dijo Judge el miércoles. «Pero tras analizarlo, pensé que lo correcto era salir del juego para no perjudicar al equipo en el campo ni en las bases».
Ha sido una temporada marcada por las lesiones para Judge, el actual Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) de la Liga Americana, quien ha registrado promedios de .241/.360/.511 con 18 jonrones y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos.
Judge se perdió gran parte del verano debido a una fractura en una costilla derecha, lesión que se cree sufrió el 26 de abril en Houston. Jugó con la lesión durante aproximadamente un mes antes de ser colocado en la lista de lesionados tras un partido disputado el 31 de mayo contra los Atléticos en West Sacramento.
Sin pasar por una asignación de rehabilitación en ligas menores, Judge regresó el 8 de septiembre contra los Rockies. En seis partidos, bateó de 23-4 (.174) con un jonrón. Boone afirmó que no cuestionaría la decisión de que Judge se saltara la asignación de rehabilitación, señalando: «Estas cosas suceden, tanto si hay asignación de rehabilitación como si no. Hicimos todo lo posible para tratar de darnos a él y a nosotros mismos la mejor oportunidad de lograr un buen resultado».
Tomado de MLB.com

item.title: [MARCA] Boone’s grim Aaron Judge injury timetable clouds Yankees’ postseason hopes
item.dc:creator: Adriano Boin
item.description: - New York Yankees. Aaron Judge triggers intense panic after sudden injury exit just days into MLB return - New York Yankees. Yankee Stadium among 10 Bronx sites testing positive for deadly Legionnaires’ bacteria after 1 dies, 8 sickened Aaron Judge’s latest injury has turned a postseason question into a major uncertainty for the New York Yankees, with manager Aaron Boone unable to provide even a rough timetable for the slugger’s return. Judge was placed on the 10-day injured list Saturday after
item.content:encoded:
- New York Yankees. Aaron Judge triggers intense panic after sudden injury exit just days into MLB return
- New York Yankees. Yankee Stadium among 10 Bronx sites testing positive for deadly Legionnaires’ bacteria after 1 dies, 8 sickened
Aaron Judge’s latest injury has turned a postseason question into a major uncertainty for the New York Yankees, with manager Aaron Boone unable to provide even a rough timetable for the slugger’s return.
Judge was placed on the 10-day injured list Saturday after an MRI revealed a right calf strain. The move comes only days after the Yankees captain returned from a lengthy absence caused by a right rib fracture.
He rejoined the lineup on Sept. 8 against the Colorado Rockies after missing more than three months.
His comeback had already been a work in progress. Judge went 4-for-23 with a home run and 11 strikeouts across his first six games back, before lower-leg discomfort forced him out of Wednesday’s 5-4 loss to the Minnesota Twins. 
The Yankees subsequently learned he had suffered the calf strain.
Boone was cautious when asked whether Judge could be available for the playoffs.
“I don’t have a timeline on it,’’ Boone said. “I can’t predict anything. … I mean, we have no idea; we’re in the early stages. We’ll just obviously treat it and see what transpires.”
“Hopefully, we can have him be an option at some point.’’
The uncertainty is particularly concerning given how little time remains before October and how recently Judge returned from his previous injury.
Yankees face October uncertainty without their captain
The timing leaves New York with little margin for error. The Yankees have already clinched a postseason berth, but they’re still chasing Tampa Bay in the American League East.
With their playoff position taking shape, every remaining game carries importance, particularly if New York wants to improve its position before the Wild Card Series.
Former Yankees manager Joe Girardi also described the injury as a significant concern, particularly because Judge had only recently returned and was still trying to regain his timing at the plate.
"Well there's a huge level of concern," Girardi said. "Because they were talking about putting him on the IL and he won't have a chance to play in anymore games this season.
“And he was not to me, ready too go from a timing standpoint and how do you get your timing you gotta play games. So it's a pretty big concern to me.”
Judge remains one of baseball’s most important offensive pieces, and his 2026 numbers currently stand at a .241 batting average with 18 home runs and 41 RBIs in 66 games. 
Even after missing significant time, his presence changes the way opposing pitchers approach the Yankees’ lineup.
New York has already learned how to navigate extended stretches without its captain, but October presents a different challenge. 
A postseason series offers less room for an offense to overcome the absence of its premier hitter, especially against teams with strong pitching.
Boone’s message is essentially wait and see. Judge will receive treatment, and the Yankees hope he can become an option at some point. However, the manager’s refusal to establish a timetable underlines how uncertain the situation remains.
The Yankees don’t need Judge back immediately to reach October, but they’ll surely want clarity before the postseason begins.

item.dc:creator: Gabe Lacques
item.description: Aaron Judge to IL with calf strain, likely to miss rest of regular season Aaron Judge was placed on the 10-day injured list with a right calf strain, the New York Yankees announced Saturday, Sept. 19, likely ending his regular season only seven games into his return from a 75-game absence due to a rib fracture. item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge to IL with calf strain, likely to miss rest of regular season
Aaron Judge was placed on the 10-day injured list with a right calf strain, the New York Yankees announced Saturday, Sept. 19, likely ending his regular season only seven games into his return from a 75-game absence due to a rib fracture.
Judge, the 34-year-old three-time American League MVP, left the Yankees' game at Minnesota on Wednesday with what the Yankees called lower leg tightness. His move to the IL was officially made on Saturday, and Max Schuemann was called up.
Judge would be eligible to return on Sunday, Sept. 27, the final day of the regular season. A return then would be unlikely, but at least Judge could return during the club's likely AL wild-card series matchup against the Boston Red Sox.
That would depend on his body cooperating. Judge was limited to 66 games this season, and injuries prompted the Yankees to acquire outfielder Heliot Ramos and infielder Luis Garcia Jr. at the August trade deadline. Center fielder Trent Grisham is also returning from a hamstring injury and manager Aaron Boone said it was unlikely Grisham will return before the regular season ends.
Like Judge, they can only hope he's ready to go when the playoff lights come on.
Other than the COVID-19 shortened 2020 season and his 27-game debut in 2016, Judge's 66 games played in 2026 marks the only other time in his 11-year career he failed to play at least 100 games. He hit 18 home runs in 237 at-bats, giving him 386 for his career. The Yankees clinched at least a wild-card berth Tuesday, one day before Judge suffered his calf injury.
In 2025, Judge won his second consecutive AL MVP, leading the major leagues in batting average (.331), on-base percentage (.457) and slugging (.688).

item.content:encoded:
Cam Schlittler has all but wrapped up the American League Cy Young Award.
The Pinstriped phenom is a -25000 favorite to become the seventh Yankee to win the honor at bet365 Sportsbook, and the biggest prediction markets, Kalshi and Polymarket, have him priced at 96 percent. There are no sure things in baseball nor in betting, but this one is pretty darn close.
While Schlittler will be making room for at least one award this winter, a debate has begun to spark up about whether the 25-year-old should also garner heavy consideration for another: AL MVP.
No pitcher has won the award in either league since Clayton Kershaw did so for the Dodgers in 2014.
Kershaw’s stat line that season was impeccable. He went 21-3, pitched to a 1.77 ERA and 0.86 WHIP, and racked up 239 strikeouts against just 31 walks in 198 1/3 innings. By season’s end, the future Hall-of-Famer had a WAR of 8.2.
Plenty has changed in baseball in the 12 years since Kershaw dominated the league, but Schlittler’s resume pops just as much. He leads the league in innings pitched, ERA, WHIP, and scoreless starts, and he’s second in strikeouts and quality starts. His 5.9 WAR at FanGraphs lags behind just Kansas City’s Bobby Witt Jr. (6.5) and Houston’s Yordan Alvarez (6.0) in the American League.
Alvarez, who was a Triple Crown threat for much of the year, is the -4000 favorite to be named AL MVP. Schlittler is currently priced at 50/1 at bet365 Sportsbook, making him the third-favorite, sandwiched between Tampa Bay’s Junior Caminero and Witt Jr.
Caminero, who leads the American League with 41 home runs, is 14/1. Witt is 125/1.
Those odds suggest that the race is over. At -4000, Alvarez owns a 97.6-percent implied probability. Kalshi has it a shade lower at 89 percent. If that was the case, why did the Schlitter-for-MVP talks get so loud that his teammates shared their thoughts?
The answer is because the right-hander has a legitimate claim to the award. Not only by the numbers, but also by the literal meaning of the award. Who was the most valuable player to his team in 2026?
With Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, and Carlos Rodon all injured for large chunks of the season, Schlittler was the only Yankee starter that Aaron Boone was able to send out every five days. He took that responsibility head-on in his second season in the majors, delivering a 1.95 ERA, 0.90 WHIP, and 228 strikeouts in 184 2/3 innings so far.
Without that level of dominance, the Yankees could be scrapping for a wild-card spot; instead, they’re still in the hunt for the best record in the American League.
Schlittler has two starts remaining, likely against the Diamondbacks on Saturday and a potentially massive one versus the Rays on Thursday. If he is able to replicate what he did in his most recent outing against the Mets in those final two appearances, he’ll have plenty of voters thinking long and hard about whether he deserves this award.
At 50/1 odds this late in the season, it’s a chance worth taking.
The Play: Cam Schlittler to win AL MVP (50/1, bet365)
Why Trust New York Post Betting
Michael Leboff is a long-suffering Islanders fan, but a long-profiting sports bettor with 10 years of experience in the gambling industry. He loves using game theory to help punters win bracket pools, find long shots, and learn how to beat the market in mainstream and niche sports.

item.title: [CBS Sports] Three questions for Aaron Judge and the Yankees as injury casts doubt on slugger's playoff availability
item.dc:creator: Mike Axisa
item.description: Friday was a bad day for the New York Yankees even though they opened their final road series of the regular season with a blowout win (NYY 9, ARI 2). Captain Aaron Judge is less than two weeks after returning from a fractured rib that sidelined him more than three months. Judge's status for the rest of the season is up in the air. item.content:encoded:
Friday was a bad day for the New York Yankees even though they opened their final road series of the regular season with a blowout win (NYY 9, ARI 2). Captain Aaron Judge is less than two weeks after returning from a fractured rib that sidelined him more than three months. Judge's status for the rest of the season is up in the air.
"I don't have a timeline on him. I'm not going to predict anything. We'll just obviously treat it and see what transpires," manager Aaron Boone said (via MLB.com). "... The reality is, we've had to play a lot of the season this year without him. There's no replacing a player who is as great as Aaron Judge, but we have high expectations. Those don't change now."
The Yankees are always cagey about Judge's injuries. They declined to reveal the severity of the calf strain or give a timetable for his return. Generally speaking, Grade 1 calf strains (the least severe) require 2-3 weeks on the injured list, though calves are very tricky and easy to reinjury. They must be allowed to heal fully, otherwise you risk a more severe injury.
For all intents and purposes, the Yankees are locked into the top wild-card spot. They're six games up in the loss column on the Boston Red Sox, who currently sit in the second wild card spot, plus the Yankees won the season series and have the tiebreaker, so it's really a seven-game lead. New York can clinch the top wild-card spot as soon as Sunday.
The AL East title remains mathematically possible, but it is a long shot. The Yankees are four games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the loss column with four head-to-head games remaining next week in the Bronx. The Rays only need to win one of those four games to clinch the season series and secure the tiebreaker, upping the difficulty for New York.
Just to lay it all out, here's what needs to happen for the Yankees to win the AL East, assuming they sweep those four games against the Rays and clinch the tiebreaker for themselves, which is a pretty big assumption:
- Rays go 6-3 or better: Rays win AL East
- Rays go 5-4: Yankees must go 9-0
- Rays go 4-5: Yankees must go 8-1
- Rays go 3-6: Yankees must go 7-2
- Rays go 2-7: Yankees must go 6-3
- Rays go 1-8: Yankees must go 5-4
- Rays go 0-9: Yankees must go 4-5
The Yankees have already clinched a postseason spot and winning the AL East was a long shot even with Judge. These last nine regular-season games are almost meaningless. If the AL East race gets interesting in a few days, the Yankees can shift gears, but the big picture takes priority this next week. Resting key relievers, lining up the rotation for the Wild Card Series, etc.
"Missing Judge, it hurts. We all know he's the best hitter in the game," Cody Bellinger said (via MLB.com). "For us in here, our mindset is, we're going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I'm fully confident that we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win, and beat anybody."
With the postseason less than two weeks away, Judge's calf injury creates a lot of questions for both him and the Yankees overall. Here are three questions for the man himself, and his team.
Three questions for Judge
1. Will he return for the postseason? This is really the only question, right? The Yankees are built around Judge being the best hitter in the world, and when he's not, the walls begin to cave in. New York had one of the lowest-scoring offenses in baseball when Judge was out with his rib injury. To paraphrase another New York baseball legend, Judge is the straw that stirs the drink.
Judge is eligible to come off the injured list next Sunday, the final day of the regular season. Roster-wise, he can return in time for the postseason. Health-wise, we have no idea. Calf strains are rarely 10-day absences, but that's what the Yankees have to hope is the case here. There's a very real chance the Yankees are without Judge for at least the Wild Card Series, and maybe longer.
“I’d like to be back by the postseason,” Aaron Judge said. “That’s definitely the plan.”
Said the calf strain involves the soleus muscle — which he said is more crucial to running and hitting — making it more difficult to play through.
2. Will he be himself at the plate? Judge did not go on a minor-league rehab assignment before returning from the rib injury and it showed. He went 4 for 23 (.174) with one walk and 13 strikeouts in his seven games back before the calf injury. His timing was not there at all. Judge's one homer came on a hanging breaking ball. Otherwise, pitchers threw fastballs by him consistently.
To put a number on it, Judge missed with 41% of his swings against fastballs in his seven games back, more than double the 19% league average. This is what it looks like when you miss with more than two out of every five swings against heaters:
It is not exactly a surprise a hitter who did not go on a rehab assignment after spending more than three months on the shelf looked out of sorts at the plate. Judge and the Yankees knew it would take him some time to get back up to speed at the plate, and they were willing to live with it. The goal was always to be ready for the postseason, not so much the regular season.
These last nine games aren't particularly important for the Yankees in the standings, but they were incredibly important to Judge. He needed at-bats to rediscover his timing at the plate, and get back to being the dominant hitter he's been throughout his career. The calf strain puts that on pause. Judge now has even fewer at-bats available to get back to being himself.
3. Will he be able to play the field? There is a scenario in which Judge plays through the calf strain as a full-time DH who doesn't run at 100% (or close to it). How the Yankees would align their defense in that scenario, I have no idea. Ben Rice is a full-time DH these days and also New York's best non-Judge hitter. Platoon-mates Luis Gárcia Jr. and Paul Goldschmidt are first basemen.
Unless the Yankees do something unexpected, like put Gárcia back at second base (where he was terrible defensively) or Rice back behind the plate (where he was also terrible defensively), slotting Judge in at DH means one of the team's most productive hitters will have to sit. This is something the Yankees will worry about when the time comes, and not a second sooner.
Three questions for the Yankees
1. Where will the righty pop come from? The Yankees have a very lefty-heavy lineup and Judge's righty heft provides important balance. Only the Cleveland Guardians have gotten fewer plate appearances from righties this season. Friday's lineup against Arizona Diamondbacks lefty Eduardo Rodriguez could be what the Yankees run out there against lefties in October:
- 1B Paul Goldschmidt, RHB
- LF Cody Bellinger, LHB
- RF Heliot Ramos, RHB
- DH Ben Rice, LHB
- 3B Amed Rosario, RHB
- CF Spencer Jones, LHB
- SS George Lombard Jr., RHB
- C Austin Wells, LHB
- 2B Anthony Volpe, RHB
Goldschmidt and Ramos are lefty mashers. Bellinger and Rice are very productive left-on-left hitters. Jones has performed well against lefties as a big leaguer, though his minor-league track record against southpaws isn't great. Rosario is having his worst season against lefties. The 7-8-9 spots are unlikely to make an impact offensively, regardless of the pitcher's handedness.
That lineup would look much more imposing with Judge in the No. 3 spot. Perhaps this is not such a big concern though? Since trade deadline day, the Yankees have the highest batting average (.289) and on-base percentage (.362) against lefties, and the third-highest slugging percentage (.456) despite Judge not playing much, and not being much of a factor when he did play.
In all likelihood the Yankees will host the Red Sox in the Wild Card Series, and Boston has three quality lefty starters (Jake Bennett, Ranger Suárez, Payton Tolle) and a shutdown lefty relief tandem (Aroldis Chapman, Erik Miller). To beat the Red Sox, the Yankees will need their righty hitters to produce, and now the status of their best right-handed hitter is in question.
2. Will the pitching hold up? Despite not having Judge for more than three months, the Yankees have the American League's best run differential (+143) and second-best record (89-64). They can thank their pitching staff. New York has allowed only 3.68 runs per game this year, the fewest in baseball. Since trade deadline day, it's an incredible 3.37 runs allowed per game.
There are some cracks beginning to form, however. Gerrit Cole has surrendered eight home runs in his last three starts, including five on a four-seam fastball that is no longer the dominant pitch it was at his peak. Max Fried's velocity has been down a tick since returning from a bone bruise in his elbow late last month. That injury has sent him to the injured list twice this year.
Cam Schlittler, the AL Cy Young favorite, has thrown a career-high 184 ⅔ innings with two regular-season starts remaining, plus the postseason. Key late-inning relievers Paul Blackburn, David Bednar, and Brent Headrick have worked a lot -- A LOT -- this season and have all shown a slight dip in velocity in recent weeks, which perhaps is a sign the workload is catching up to them.
Without Judge (and sometimes even with him), the Yankees are a run prevention team. Their superpower is a suffocating pitching staff that is among the best in baseball at limiting hard contact, particularly in the air. With Judge absent, the pitching staff and the ability to prevent runs in general will be of paramount importance. No Judge reduces the margin of error considerably.
3. What about their other injured players? Judge is not the only injured Yankee. Center field Trent Grisham has not played since Sept. 4 due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain. On Friday, Boone said Grisham is pretty far into his running program, and he could make it back before the end of the regular season. That would give the outfield a lift should Judge miss extended time.
Second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. has not played since jamming his thumb sliding into second base on Sept. 8. Boone said Chisholm will come off the injured list when the Yankees return home next week. He's had a down year overall, but Chisholm was playing his best baseball of the season right before the injury. He's an important presence given his speed and defense in particular.
Left-hander Ryan Weathers is working his way back from a flexor strain. He last pitched Aug. 22. Weathers is throwing bullpen sessions, though Boone confirmed he won't return during the regular season. If/when Weathers does return, it will be as a reliever. He has bullpen experience and the Yankees could use middle relief help, but Weathers has to make it back first.
At minimum, Chisholm and Grisham would give the Yankees more options for their Judge-less lineup, even if they only platoon. It wouldn't be hard to find a role for Weathers, who had allowed no more than one run in six of his last seven starts before the injury. Bottom line though, the Yankees need Judge. Everything else is secondary to his return and effectiveness.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Gerrit Cole Slowly Easing Yankees’ Postseason Concerns With Diamondbacks Start

With the postseason weeks away for the New York Yankees, Cole, who should be their two starter heading into the postseason, allowed seven home runs and nine earned runs in 11.1 IP. If there were any questions about Cole's abilities, his s
item.content:encoded:
Gerrit Cole's two-game stretch against the San Diego Padres and the New York Mets raised concerns. With the postseason weeks away for the New York Yankees, Cole, who should be their two starter heading into the postseason, allowed seven home runs and nine earned runs in 11.1 IP. It was a ghastly set of performances, and it may have left the organization wondering how the rest of the season would shake out for their former Cy Young winner.
If there were any questions about Cole's abilities, his start against the 80-74 Arizona Diamondbacks may have alleviated a few worries. It may also have put to rest any internal debates. Cole did allow a home run this time out, but it was just one. Corbin Carroll pulled a 388-foot home run off Cole's bat at 110.7 MPH.
Headed into the postseason, pitching in Game 1 is an easy decision. Aaron Boone needs to hand the ball to Cy Young frontrunner and prospective MVP candidate Cam Schlittler. There's no reason to really overthink that one.
If Cole starts struggling again, though, the question of who the second starter is gets a little trickier. That might still be a conversation worth having if things go differently to close out the year, but for now, if Cole pitches the way he did against the Diamondbacks, there's no reason to save him for another series.
Cole's big test will be against the Tampa Bay Rays, since he lines up to face them in their next series. If he pitches well against them, he'll further solidify his spot as the team's two-starter.
A better outing for Gerrit Cole
When Aaron Boone was asked about Cole after the game, he said he wasn't too worried. He chalked his struggles up to a long season.
"I think a lot of people probably overreacted to a couple of outings that, frankly, are inevitable in a long season," Boone said, according to the New York Post's Greg Joyce. "The reality is he's having an outstanding season, he's throwing the ball really well, and a great pitcher like him is going to be able to make some adjustments when you have a couple where they get to you."
The Carroll blast was Cole's lone blemish. He pitched six innings of two-run ball, striking out six, allowing no walks, and four hits.
On the back end, he gave up a ton of soft contact. The Diamondbacks had an average exit velocity of 86.8 MPH against him. That's way down from his last two starts, when batters averaged 96.8 MPH against him.
This is the type of Cole the Yankees need in the postseason. Who knows what's happening with Aaron Judge, so the rotation and bullpen have to essentially be perfect if this team is going to make any noise this postseason.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

item.content:encoded:
By Field Level Media
Sep 19 (Field Level Media) – The New York Yankees placed outfielder Aaron Judge on the 10-day injured list Saturday due to a right calf strain.
The move is retroactive to Thursday, one day after the Yankees’ captain and three-time American League MVP was removed from a game against the Minnesota Twins after the sixth inning due to tightness in his lower right leg.
Judge told reporters afterward that he felt the injury during the first inning and “tried to play it off” before reporting it to manager Aaron Boone.
Also on Saturday, the Yankees recalled infielder/outfielder Max Schuemann from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre.
Judge, 34, missed more than three months of the season due to a rib injury and only returned on Sept. 8.
“Once you start ramping up, things pop up,” Judge said. “Hopefully, it’s just one little thing and we’re back out there soon.”
Because the move is backdated to Thursday, Judge would be eligible for activation on Sept. 27, the final day of the regular season.
Judge has appeared in just 66 games this season, batting .241 with 18 home runs and 41 RBIs. In his seven games back from his previous IL stint, he was just 4-for-23 (.174) with one homer and three RBIs.
Schuemann, 29, batted .194 with two homers and eight RBIs in 41 games earlier this season with the Yankees.
(–Field Level Media)

item.dc:creator: Santiago Tovar

That makes Cam Schlittler’s dominant breakout campaign all the more remarkable—so much so that manager Aaron Boone believes the young right-hander has built a compelling case to take home the American League Cy Young Award. When asked about Schlittler’s transformative presence in the rotation, Boone didn’t mince words: “Well, he’s gonna win the Cy Young!” The manager’s rin
item.content:encoded:
For a historic franchise like the New York Yankees, rotation stability is paramount over the long haul of a 162-game season. That makes Cam Schlittler’s dominant breakout campaign all the more remarkable—so much so that manager Aaron Boone believes the young right-hander has built a compelling case to take home the American League Cy Young Award.
When asked about Schlittler’s transformative presence in the rotation, Boone didn’t mince words: “Well, he’s gonna win the Cy Young!” The manager’s ringing endorsement underscores just how dominant Schlittler has been on the mound this year.
While Boone continues to navigate rotation depth with Ryan Weathers sidelined for the remainder of the regular season, Schlittler gives the Yankees a legitimate ace to rely on as they gear up for October.
On the offensive side, Boone is also monitoring the return timeline for slugger Aaron Judge, who was sidelined with a calf strain. In the meantime, the Yankees skipper has relied on depth options like Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger to keep the lineup producing.
Key milestones driving Schlittler’s Cy Young case
A stellar 2026 breakout campaign with the Yankees has vaulted Schlittler directly into the front-runner conversation for the American League Cy Young Award. Stepping up as the de facto ace while Gerrit Cole missed time, Schlittler has delivered elite run suppression, swing-and-miss stuff, and exceptional durability.
Here is a breakdown of the key numbers and milestones anchoring Schlittler’s Cy Young candidacy:
- 1.95 ERA: Schlittler took over the MLB ERA lead in September, standing as the only qualified starter with an ERA under 2.00.
- Historical run: His 1.71 ERA through his first 16 starts marked the lowest ERA by a Yankees starter through that stretch since Hall of Famer Whitey Ford in 1964.
- 228 Strikeouts in 184.2 IP (11.1 K/9): Schlittler eclipsed the 200-strikeout mark on August 28 against Boston, becoming the fourth-youngest pitcher in franchise history to achieve the feat.
- Signature outings: Highlighted by a career-high 13-strikeout performance against the Cincinnati Reds on June 19, along with double-digit strikeout shutouts against Philadelphia (12 K) and Atlanta (11 K).
Other top Cy Young contenders
Schlittler isn’t running unopposed in a tightly contested American League race. Strong campaigns from power arm Dylan Cease of the Toronto Blue Jays and left-hander Garrett Crochet of the Boston Red Sox keep them firmly in the mix.
Over in the National League, the Cy Young field features plenty of heavy hitters, headlined by Milwaukee Brewers phenom Jacob Misiorowski, Atlanta Braves veteran Chris Sale, and the Philadelphia Phillies duo of Cristopher Sanchez and Jesus Luzardo.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees were dealt another major injury blow earlier this week, and it came at the worst possible time in the MLB season.
Days later, on Saturday, the team placed Aaron Judge officially back on the injured list with a right calf strain, just 11 days after returning from a lengthy absence caused by a fractured rib.
At the same time, however, the Yankees received encouraging news on Jazz Chisholm Jr., who could be back in the lineup before the end of the regular season.
Aaron Judge heads back to injured list
Sep 11, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees right fielder Aaron Judge (99) runs back to the dugout in the sixth inning against the New York Mets at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
The Yankees announced Saturday that Judge was placed on the 10-day injured list, retroactive to Sept. 17, with a right calf strain. New York recalled infielder/outfielder Max Schuemann from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre to take his roster spot.
Judge first experienced tightness in his lower right leg during Wednesday's game against the Minnesota Twins and was removed after the sixth inning. An MRI performed Thursday revealed the calf strain.
The bigger concern is the timing. Judge only returned Sept. 8 after missing more than three months with his rib injury. He went 4-for-23 with one home run across six games following his return.
Manager Aaron Boone has not provided a timetable for Judge's return and would not speculate about whether he will be available for the postseason. His earliest possible return is Sept. 27, the final day of the regular season.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. could return next week
Jun 2, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (13) walks off the field after the top of the seventh inning against the Cleveland Guardians at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
The Yankees did receive some positive injury news regarding Chisholm, who has been sidelined with a sprained right thumb since Sept. 10.
Boone said Chisholm is "doing well" and should be activated during the team's current homestand. MLB reports that Chisholm has hit for four consecutive days and has also resumed throwing, putting him on track for a potential return around Sept. 22-24.
That would give the Yankees a much-needed boost, particularly with Judge now sidelined again. New York is chasing Tampa Bay in the AL East and has a crucial four-game series against the Rays next week.
The Yankees now face the difficult task of navigating the final stretch of the regular season without their captain while hoping Chisholm can return as expected.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] New York Yankees’ Aaron Boone Makes Bold Ben Rice Statement Amid Diamondbacks Series
item.dc:creator: Jackson Kruse
item.description: Designated hitter Ben Rice hit his 39th home run of the season as the New York Yankees beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 at Chase Field in Phoenix on Friday night. He's been great. You look up at his num
item.content:encoded:
Designated hitter Ben Rice hit his 39th home run of the season as the New York Yankees beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 at Chase Field in Phoenix on Friday night.
Following the win, Yankees manager Aaron Boone claimed he predicted Rice would hit 39 home runs this year.
New York Yankees Manager Aaron Boone Made Bold Ben Rice Prediction That Came True
"Thirty-nine [home runs] was my prediction. I swear. So I'm hoping he goes sailing on by that," Boone said. He's been great. You look up at his numbers, and it's an elite season. Really here of late, over the last three or four weeks, after a little bit of a lull there, he's found his stride again. I feel like he's having great at-bats every night."
"39 was my prediction!"
Aaron Boone tells @M_Marakovits he anticipated a big year from Ben Rice at the beginning of the season. pic.twitter.com/iMNLIOK3FE
— YES Network (@YESNetwork) September 19, 2026
Rice, 27, is having the best season of his young career. He made his first career All-Star Game this season and has posted 3.6 bWAR and an .897 OPS with 39 home runs and 94 RBI over 146 games.
Rice was asked if he knew about Boone's preseason prediction after the win.
"Yeah, he said something in spring training I feel like. 'We really want you to get out there and hit 39 [home runs] for us.' So I know what he was doing," Rice said. "He was trying to get under my skin a little bit. He likes to short you one short you two of maybe what your goal would be."
New York Yankees Right Now
The Yankees' record improved to 89-64 after Friday's win over the Diamondbacks.
New York has a 5 1/2-game lead over the Boston Red Sox for the top Wild Card spot.
In the division standings, New York is four games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for first place in the AL East.
Next, the Yankees are slated to play the Diamondbacks at 8:10 p.m. EDT on Saturday. The series will wrap up on Sunday afternoon.
The Yankees will finish the season by hosting the Tampa Bay Rays for four games, and then the Baltimore Orioles for three games.
If the standings hold up, the Yankees will host the Red Sox in the Wild Card round.

item.title: [roundtable.io] Yankees' Gerrit Cole Still Has a Very Alarming Problem
item.dc:creator: Matthew Schmidt

item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees pitcher Gerrit Cole still has a very big problem heading into the MLB playoffs.
Cole allowed four hits while registering six strikeouts, and his control remained sharp without any walks. He did surrender yet another home run, but for the most part, this was a solid outing by the right-hander.
Cole generated just six swings-and-misses on 62 strikes against the Diamondbacks, marking a 15 percent whiff rate. And while that was better than his eight percent rate against the New York Mets in his preceding start, it's still not good.
In fact, on the season as a whole, Cole has posted a 21.3 percent whiff rate, which places him in the 18th percentile in baseball.
Cole has been declining in that area for quite some time now, but this season has been particularly bad in that department.
Now, thanks to Cole's pinpoint control and his ability to paint corners, he still owns a 9.1 K/9 rate this year, a testament to just how good of a pitcher he is.
And while his average fastball velocity (96.8 mph) still ranks in the 85th percentile, his secondary stuff is simply not as lethal anymore.
Cole has still managed to log a 3.63 ERA in spite of his question marks this season, but the days of him being a bona fide ace appear to be over.
It also begs the question of whether or not he would be the Yankees' best option for a No. 2 starter in the playoffs. We know that Cam Schlittler will be the lead arm. But will Cole get the nod over Max Fried? An argument can even be made for Carlos Rodon, who has been very good when healthy this season.
Chances are, Aaron Boone will hand the No. 2 job to Cole because he's Gerrit Cole and because he has been good for most of 2026. But the fact that Cole's stuff is clearly declining — and right before the postseason — is a major concern.
Cole is smart enough where he can find ways to work around his ace stuff no longer being there. We just saw it in Arizona on Friday night. But can the Yankees trust him enough at this stage to get a pivotal Game 2 start?
We're about to find out.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees news: Aaron Boone drops hugely discouraging Aaron Judge update after IL move appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees are back in the playoffs, but will Aaron Judge join them?
Just after returning from a three-month absence, Judge was placed on the 1o-day injured list with a right calf strain. With October around the corner, Yankees manager Aaron Boone gave a bleak outlook on whether Judge will return, per Bob Nightengale of USA Today.
When asked if Judge will return for the playoffs, he said, "I don't know.''
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
"I don't have a timeline on it,'' Boone said. "I can't predict anything. … I mean, we have no idea; we're in the early stages. We'll just obviously treat it and see what transpires."
"Hopefully, we can have him be an option at some point.''
For three months, Judge was out with a rib injury. He returned to the lineup on Sept. 8 against the Colorado Rockies.
From there, Judge went 4-for-23 with 13 strikeouts. Then, Judge experienced leg discomfort during the three-game series against the Minnesota Twins. He last appeared on Wednesday, going 0-for-2 in a 5-4 loss to the Twins.
The Yankees are 89-64 and are leading the American League Wild Card standings. To win the Wild Card, the Magic need six wins with nine games left.
Making it through October without Judge will be a challenge.
"The reality is that we've had to play a lot of the season this year without him,'' Boone said. "There's no replacing a player as great as Aaron Judge, but you know we have high expectations that don't change now. We have a lot of confidence in the people we run out there every day. We're going to match up day in and day out, and the goal doesn't change.''
Judge is batting .241 with 57 hits, 18 home runs, and 41 RBIs.

item.content:encoded:
On Saturday, the New York Yankees will play the second game of their series with the Arizona Diamondbacks in Phoenix.
They are coming off a 9-2 win on Friday.
Ahead of Saturday’s game, the Yankees will place three-time MVP Aaron Judge on the injured list.
Gary Phillips of NY Daily News Sports wrote (on Friday): “Aaron Judge will be placed on the 10-day injured list tomorrow with a right calf strain, the #Yankees say. A corresponding move will take place at that time.”
Roster Move Admits How Yankees Feel About Domínguez
It’s been revealed that the Yankees will use the open roster spot (from Judge) to call up Max Schuemann.
Bryan Hoch of MLB.com wrote (on Friday): “Aaron Boone said he would not place a timeline on Aaron Judge’s calf strain. Asked if Judge would be back for the postseason, Boone said, “I don’t know. I’m not going to predict anything.” Max Schuemann is en route and will join the Yankees tomorrow.”
It’s fair to point out that Jasson Domínguez (who was recently sent to Triple-A) would have been a good option.
He has started in right field 42 times this year.
Here’s what people were saying:
@RealPaulyRyder: “Dominguez is crushing the ball, but Schumann is coming up…”
@JackMcTraddles: “Do they not want to waste a Dominguez option or do they really like Schuemann more?”

item.content:encoded:
The Bronx Bombers secured their spot in the 2026 MLB postseason, but it hasn’t all been smooth sailing. Cody Bellinger lamented Aaron Judge’s recent injury, which has left the New York Yankees awaiting an update on his timeline, but he remains confident in the roster’s talent and its ability to keep moving forward.
“Missing Judge, it hurts. We all know he’s the best hitter in the game,” Bellinger said via MLB insider Bryan Hoch on X. “For us in here, our mindset is, we’re going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I’m fully confident that we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win, and beat anybody.”
The Pinstripes want to return to the World Series, and they will have to do it with the players available to them. For now, Aaron Boone has both depth and talent on his roster to accomplish big things in the Bronx.
What injury did Aaron Judge suffer?
Aaron Judge is back on the injured list after suffering a right calf strain during Wednesday’s game against the Minnesota Twins. He initially left the game early with leg tightness, but an MRI revealed the strain, forcing the Yankees to put him back on the 10-day IL.
Aaron Judge #99 of the New York Yankees looks on.
Making matters worse, he had just returned a week prior from a broken rib that kept him out for over three months. While he could technically be eligible to return for the regular-season finale on September 27, Aaron Boone hasn’t set a timeline, leaving his availability for the postseason up in the air.
Bellinger steps into a bigger role
With Aaron Judge sidelined, Cody Bellinger must step up as the primary offensive anchor and versatile anchor for the New York Yankees. Batting .273 with 16 home runs, 71 RBIs, and an .788 OPS across 126 games, Bellinger brings crucial run production to the middle of the order.
His elite defensive flexibility will be just as vital, as he is expected to shift seamlessly between right field to cover Judge’s usual post, center field, and first base depending on daily lineup needs.
Cody Bellinger at the 2026 MLB All-Star Game.
Yankees’ next challenges
As the regular season wraps up, Cody Bellinger and the Yankees are heading into the home stretch with a busy final week on the schedule. They finish up their road trip out west with two more against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field (September 19 and 20), before returning to the Bronx for a heavy home stand.
They’ll kick that off with a four-game set against the Tampa Bay Rays at Yankee Stadium—including a Tuesday doubleheader on September 22—and then wrap up the regular season at home with a three-game series against the Baltimore Orioles from September 25 to 27.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees will play the rest of the regular season without slugger Aaron Judge. While they understand the magnitude of his loss, they enter the stretch run with belief.
The Yanks scored five runs in the first inning of a 9-2 victory over the Arizona Diamondbacks in the first game of a weekend series Friday, and the teams meet again Saturday in Phoenix as Arizona attempts to stay alive in the National League wild-card race.
"Obviously losing 'Judgey' hurts," Cody Bellinger said. "We all know he's the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is we're going to have to find a way. The talent in this room speaks for itself.
"I'm fully confident we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win and beat anybody."
American League Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95 ERA) will face Arizona right-hander Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.77) in the second game of the series.
The Diamondbacks (80-74) will ask Pfaadt to end a slump in which they have lost five of six. They are five games behind San Diego, the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia (all 85-69) for the three NL wild-card spots with eight games to play.
"We know where we're at," Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said. "We can't afford to worry about things we can't control. I'm going to say there's time. There's always time."
The Yankees (89-64) are 48-39 this season without Judge, who was placed on the injured list Friday with a strained right calf after missing three months earlier with a fractured right rib.
New York is also without injured regulars Jazz Chisholm Jr. (thumb) and Trent Grisham (hamstring), although manager Aaron Boone said Chisholm could return for the Tampa Bay series early next week.
The Yankees, who already have qualified for the postseason, are four games behind Tampa Bay in the AL East, and the teams have a four-game series at Yankee Stadium beginning Tuesday.
"There is no replacing a player as great as Aaron Judge, but we have high expectations that don't change now," Boone said. "One thing we do know is that we are in the dance.
"We've been built on the strength of our starting pitching all year."
No one has been as strong as Schlittler, who is in his first full season and has made every start while Max Fried, Gerrit Cole and Carlos Rodon have missed time with injuries or recovery time.
Schlittler has won four of his last five starts and has given up one run or fewer in each of his last seven. He was struck on the back of his right leg by Bo Bichette's 111.5 mph comebacker on his 94th and last pitch of a 2-0 victory over the New York Mets last Sunday, but shrugged it off.
"You have an ace at the top that has pitched like that," Boone said. "That's a good place to start. He's been dominant. This is largely in line with who we saw down the stretch last year."
Schlittler has never faced the Diamondbacks, although Jesus Sanchez is 4 for 12 with three walks against him.
Pfaadt is 0-2 with a 5.74 ERA in his last five starts, and he gave up six runs and 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings in a loss to Texas on Aug. 12. He will be pitching on six days' rest after being pushed back so Eduardo Rodriguez could start the first game of the series.
Pfaadt lost his only outing against the Yankees, giving up six runs in 4 1/3 innings of a 7-1 loss as a rookie in 2023. Cody Bellinger is 2 for 7 with two solo homers against him and Luis Garcia Jr. is 3 for 7 with a homer.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Yankees Are Creating Their Own Distraction With Aaron Judge Injury Secrecy
item.dc:creator: Joseph Randazzo; Unknown
item.description: The New York Yankees haven't exactly been forthright about what's been going on with Aaron Judge. They didn't offer much information when he was initially pulled during the game against the Minnesota Twins. All the public knew was that Judge had tightness in his lower leg, and that was about it. They didn't alleviate any concerns about Judge after he was placed on the injured list. In fact, things have been just as hush. According to the Daily News' Gary Phillips, Judge wasn't available to speak
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees haven't exactly been forthright about what's been going on with Aaron Judge. They didn't offer much information when he was initially pulled during the game against the Minnesota Twins. All the public knew was that Judge had tightness in his lower leg, and that was about it.
They didn't alleviate any concerns about Judge after he was placed on the injured list. In fact, things have been just as hush.
According to the Daily News' Gary Phillips, Judge wasn't available to speak to the media before the game. He wasn't there for them after their 9-2 win against the Arizona Diamondbacks either. The extent of the calf strain is still unclear.
Aaron Boone didn't offer up much of an answer when asked about Judge. His response was muted and didn't offer insight into whether he'll return in the postseason.
"I don't have a timeline on him," Boone said, according to MLB.com's Bryan Hoch. "I'm not going to predict anything. We'll just obviously treat it and see what transpires."
While the public knowing what's wrong with Judge doesn't change his schedule or the organization's plans heading into the postseason, their secrecy won't keep the team from answering a barrage of questions. In fact, they'll likely get more.
This isn't the type of story that goes away with time, and even though the Yankees beat a tough opponent in Eduardo Rodriguez, that will be the story on all the back pages. There won't be an image of a sullen Rodriguez walking off the mound, but rather an image of Judge plastered on every newspaper. This storm cloud is still following the team.
Ghosting the media is a weird look, too
Plus, Judge avoiding the media looks odd when Jazz Chisholm Jr. or Clint Frazier did the same and took hits for it. When Frazier did it in 2019, a headline in The Athletic said that he "ghosted" reporters. There won't be any of that with Judge.
Not speaking to the media was held against those guys and used to say something about their character. For Judge, their captain, the same standard should apply. If he is going to be the example of how a New York Yankee should carry themselves, he should be front and center for reporters, as anyone else would be.
Obviously, Judge could talk, and the Yankees can offer a realistic timetable for what they think is happening, but that doesn't change his timeline. They'll still have to be without him, and guys like Spencer Jones will need to step up.
Still, come the postseason, it's probably better to mitigate any potential circus around the team. Playing in October is hard enough, and the team already gets enough attention during this time of year. No need to make things harder for themselves.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are getting closer to having Jazz Chisholm Jr. back in the lineup.
Manager Aaron Boone said Chisholm is expected to be activated from the 10-day injured list during New York's final regular-season homestand. The Yankees begin that homestand Tuesday against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Chisholm has been sidelined since Sept. 10 after spraining his right thumb on a head-first slide into second base against the Colorado Rockies.
The second baseman has continued making progress during his recovery. Boone said Friday marked Chisholm's fourth straight day of hitting in the batting cages, while he has also resumed throwing on the field.
The Yankees have been using Anthony Volpe at second base while Chisholm recovers. His return will give Boone another option in the infield as New York manages its lineup during the final week of the regular season.
Chisholm was also swinging the bat well before the injury. He hit .375 with a .464 on-base percentage and .500 slugging percentage over his final seven games.
The 28-year-old has appeared in 134 games this season, batting .232 with 16 doubles, three triples, 19 home runs and 55 RBI in 461 at-bats.
Chisholm has also provided plenty of value on the bases. He has scored 68 runs and stolen 40 bases on 49 attempts while posting a .312 on-base percentage and .403 slugging percentage.
His return comes at an important point for New York. The Yankees entered Saturday with an 88-64 record and sat 4 games behind the Rays in the AL East.
New York is also dealing with the expected absence of Aaron Judge for the remainder of the regular season, making Chisholm's return another potential boost for the lineup.
For now, the Yankees will continue monitoring Chisholm's thumb as he works toward activation. If he remains on schedule, he should be back during the final homestand before the postseason begins.
