item.content:encoded:
Yankees news: Gerrit Cole makes history in win vs. Diamondbacks appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
New York Yankees starter Gerrit Cole made MLB history in Friday night's 9-2 win against the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
The 36-year-old earned his 162nd career victory, moving past Mike Moore's 161 wins for the most ever by a pitcher who was selected No. 1 overall in the MLB Draft. Cole was chosen first by the Pittsburgh Pirates in 2011, while Moore went to the Seattle Mariners with the top selection in 1981. David Price is next on the list, ranking third with 157 career wins.
The milestone came as Cole bounced back after allowing seven home runs across his previous two starts, the highest two-game figure of his career. He also had surrendered leadoff home runs in each of those outings.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
After working on his delivery and potential pitch-tipping issues since his previous start against the New York Mets, Cole retired Arizona in order during a 12-pitch opening inning. Corbin Carroll later hit a two-run homer on a four-seam fastball that missed its location, but Cole gave up nothing else to the Diamondbacks.
The right-hander completed six innings, allowing two runs and four hits while issuing no walks and striking out six. He threw 90 pitches, with 62 going for strikes, finishing with a 9-9 record.
New York provided Cole with plenty of early support, sending its first five hitters to base against Eduardo Rodriguez during a five-run opening inning. Ben Rice drew a bases-loaded walk, Amed Rosario delivered an RBI single and George Lombard Jr. added a two-run single.
Rice later launched his 39th homer of the season in the third inning, while Lombard hit his own solo shot in the sixth and finished with three RBIs.
The Yankees improved to 89-64 and moved within four games of the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East with nine games remaining. New York had already secured a postseason berth and has now won 11 of its last 15 games.
Manager Aaron Boone also confirmed that Cole should receive a start if the Yankees reach the American League Wild Card Series.
Related: Yankees manager Aaron Boone drops huge Cam Schlittler Cy Young prediction

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Gerrit Cole llegó al Chase Field con mucho más en juego en su salida del viernes por la noche que el resultado final de un partido de septiembre. Los Yankees ya se habían asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero el orden de su rotación aún se estaba definiendo y a Cole solo le quedaba un pequeño margen para afianzar su puesto en ella.
Los Yankees le dieron margen de maniobra desde el principio. Cole supo aprovechar bien esa ventaja para que los Yankees se llevaran una cómoda victoria por 9-2. Lanzó seis entradas, cedió cuatro hits y dos carreras, ponchó a seis y no concedió ninguna base por bolas. El as de los Yankees lanzó 62 de 90 lanzamientos como strikes y eliminó a 13 de los últimos 15 bateadores a los que se enfrentó.
Los Yankees siguieron sumando carreras y Spencer Jones echó una mano a Cole con una atrapada en deslizamiento en la tercera entrada.
Con esta victoria, los Yankees se sitúan con un balance de 89-64, a cuatro partidos de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana y 5 1/2 partidos por delante de Boston en la lucha por la primera plaza de comodín de la Liga Americana. Dado que la serie de comodines está programada para empezar el 29 de septiembre, la última salida de Cole en la temporada regular ya no se centra tanto en acumular minutos de juego como en demostrar que la versión en la que los Yankees pueden confiar en octubre es la que está ahora en el montículo.
Los Yankees ya tienen asegurada su plaza en la postemporada, pero el equipo aún tiene que organizar una rotación sólida para una serie corta, en la que una sola salida floja puede dar al traste con toda la ronda. Cole llegó a Arizona con solo una salida más, después de esta, que pudiera influir en esa decisión.
Cole alcanza un hito que ningún número 1 del draft ha logrado nunca
No fue hasta que los Yankees sentenciaron el partido cuando la noche de Cole pasó a ocupar un lugar más destacado en la historia de la MLB. Esa victoria fue la número 162 de su carrera, lo que le permitió superar a Mike Moore como el lanzador con más victorias de todos los seleccionados en el número 1 del draft de la MLB. Pittsburgh eligió a Cole como primera elección en 2011. Moore, elegido en primer lugar por Seattle en 1981, terminó con 161 victorias. David Price ocupa el tercer puesto entre los lanzadores elegidos en el número 1 del draft, con 157.
Este hito vino acompañado de una advertencia de octubre que aún pesaba. Corbin Carroll conectó un jonrón de dos carreras en la segunda entrada con una bola rápida de cuatro costuras que no llegó donde debía. Fue el único daño que Arizona le hizo a Cole, pero ese lanzamiento fue importante por lo que había pasado justo antes del viernes.
Cole había encajado siete jonrones en sus dos últimas salidas, la mayor cantidad que había permitido nunca en un periodo de dos salidas. Cuatro de esos siete fueron con bolas rápidas de cuatro costuras. Si sumas el jonrón de Carroll, cinco de los ocho jonrones que el as de los Yankees ha encajado en sus últimas tres salidas han sido con la bola rápida de cuatro costuras.
El problema del lanzamiento de cuatro costuras se ha reducido, pero no ha desaparecido
Cole ha encajado 10 jonrones en sus últimas seis salidas, en las que ha cedido 18 carreras en 34 2/3 entradas. Su balance es de 9-9, con una efectividad de 3,63, un WHIP de 1,10 y 123 ponches frente a 22 bases por bolas en 121 1/3 entradas y 21 salidas como titular.
Antes de las malas salidas contra San Diego y los Mets, Cole tenía una efectividad de 3,29 en 18 aperturas. En las cuatro aperturas previas al viernes, los bateadores habían conseguido 16 de 48 contra su bola rápida de cuatro costuras, mientras que en sus primeras 16 aperturas habían conseguido 32 de 173 contra ella.
El as de los Yankees ha registrado una tasa de strikes fallidos del 11,6 % con su lanzamiento de cuatro costuras en las tres salidas que llevaba hasta el viernes, por debajo del 22,8 % que había logrado en sus primeras 17 salidas. Los Yankees necesitaban pruebas de que ese lanzamiento volviera a funcionar contra bateadores del nivel de la postemporada.
Boone mantiene a Cole en los planes de los Yankees para octubre
Aaron Boone ya había dejado claro que dos malas salidas no iban a dejar fuera a Cole de la rotación de los Yankees para la postemporada. Tras la derrota de los Yankees ante los Mets, Boone dejó claras sus expectativas.
«Espero que la próxima vez acierte», dijo Boone.
Lo del viernes no ha cambiado el plan general de Boone para octubre. Cuando le preguntaron si Cole debería contar con ser titular si los Yankees llegan a la Serie de Comodines, el entrenador volvió a respaldarlo.
«Sí, espero que Gerrit Cole sea el abridor», dijo Boone.
La cuestión más importante es qué versión de la bola rápida de Cole le acompañará. El analista de YES Network, David Cone, había señalado los lanzamientos secundarios, diciendo que los bateadores se habían acostumbrado a esperar la bola rápida.
«No respetan tus lanzamientos secundarios, están esperando tu bola rápida», dijo Cone.
Una salida más supone una prueba a la altura de octubre
Cole tiene prevista una salida más en la temporada regular, en casa contra los Rays la semana que viene. Esa salida puede dar a los Yankees una idea más clara antes de organizar su plantilla de lanzadores de cara a una posible serie de comodín al mejor de tres.
El viernes se dieron pasos importantes. El as de los Yankees atacó la zona de strike, no concedió ninguna base por bolas y mantuvo a raya a Arizona tras el golpe de Carroll en la segunda entrada. Además, los Yankees limitaron su carga de trabajo a 90 lanzamientos.
Pero la pregunta sobre el jonrón le siguió hasta salir del Chase Field. Cole hizo historia en la MLB y recuperó algo de confianza en la misma noche. La bola rápida de cuatro costuras aún tiene una última prueba en septiembre antes de que los Yankees decidan hasta qué punto pueden confiar en ella en octubre.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

item.title: [New York Daily News] Yankees’ Jazz Chisholm Jr. set to return on team’s final homestand

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — While Friday wasn’t a positive day in terms of injury news for the Aaron Judge-less Yankees, Aaron Boone did say that the team can count on a reinforcement soon.
That would be Jazz Chisholm Jr., who is expected to return from a sprained right thumb on the team’s upcoming and final homestand of the regular season. Boone said that Friday was the second baseman’s fourth day of hitting in a row. He’s also been throwing the last few days.
“He’s getting very close,” Boone said.
Chisholm previously said that he hoped to come off the injured list when the Yankees returned home from Arizona. He hurt his thumb while sliding into second base on Sept. 8.
Chisholm is an impending free agent in the midst of a disappointing season, but he had rounded into form before getting. He hit .295 with an .832 OPS, three home runs, 10 RBI and 10 stolen bases over his last 29 games. He also had a .391 OPS and a 1.028 OPS over his last 15 games.
The hope is that Chisholm can pick up where he left off, especially with Judge returning to the IL with a right calf strain.
Chisholm is hitting .232 with a .715 OPS, 19 home runs, 55 RBI and 40 steals overall.
GRISHAM ‘COULD BE IN PLAY’
Boone also said that Trent Grisham is pretty far into his running progression and “could be in play at the end of the season.” The center fielder suffered his second right hamstring strain of the season earlier this month.
Prior to that, Grisham hit .211 with a .703 OPS and 18 home runs. He’s also been one of the slowest and worst defensive center fielders in baseball the last two years.
With Grisham not producing on either side of the ball and Spencer Jones more than holding his own, the former was not guaranteed to start in the playoffs prior to Judge’s injury. Now, however, Grisham could play center while Jones handles right. The Yankees can also use Jones in center and Heliot Ramos is right against lefties.
WEATHERS WON’T RETURN BEFORE PLAYOFFS
While the Yankees had hoped otherwise, Aaron Boone said Ryan Weathers is “unlikely” to return before the end of the regular season. The left-handed starter, working his way back from a flexor strain as a reliever, is expected to throw his second bullpen session at Chase Field on Saturday.
Asked if the Yankees would be comfortable having Weathers’ first game off the IL come in the postseason, neither Boone nor pitching coach Matt Blake ruled the idea out.
“I don’t know if ‘comfortable’ is [the right word],” Blake said, “but it might be the course of action where he’s the best option even though he hasn’t pitched in the last three or four weeks.”

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] No Aaron Judge, no problem? Yankees show they're still a force to be reckoned with
item.dc:creator: Bob Nightengale; USA TODAY
item.description: PHOENIX — Just in case anyone thought the New York Yankees would simply fade away into the night, their season drifting out to sea with the news that Aaron Judge may be done for the season, the Bronx Bombers delivered a subtle message Friday night that reverberated around the baseball world. The Yankees, with Gerrit Cole looking more like the 2023 Cy Young winner than the pitcher who looked like he was throwing batting practice earlier this month, smacked around the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 Frid
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Just in case anyone thought the New York Yankees would simply fade away into the night, their season drifting out to sea with the news that Aaron Judge may be done for the season, the Bronx Bombers delivered a subtle message Friday night that reverberated around the baseball world.
The Yankees, with Gerrit Cole looking more like the 2023 Cy Young winner than the pitcher who looked like he was throwing batting practice earlier this month, smacked around the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 Friday, and acted afterwards as if it was simply business as usual.
There was Cole, who had given up seven homers in his last two starts pitching his best game in a month, yielding four hits and two runs in six innings.
There was DH Ben Rice, looking like a top-5 MVP candidate by hitting his 39th home run of the season − just as Yankees manager Aaron Boone predicted in spring training − to go along with 94 RBI.
There was rookie shortstop George Lombard, hitting a homer and playing flawless defense.
And there were the Yankees, talking as if they plan to be playing deep into October, whether Judge is in uniform or on their bench as a cheerleader. Judge is going on the injured list with a strained calf and the Yankees have no idea whether he'll return.
"I mean, it's a tough blow for us to take,'' Rice said. "Obviously, we were missing him for a long time there (three months), so this one is especially hard to swallow, just being back for a brief period and already gone.
"But we got no choice but to just keep playing hard, keeping doing our thing.''
Well, that starts on the mound, and with Cole dominating Friday, with Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler scheduled Saturday, and Max Fried and Carlos Rodon pitching well, there may not be a more formidable starting rotation in the postseason.
Cole, 9-9 with a 3.63 ERA in his first season back from Tommy John surgery, certainly knows there's room for improvement. But after being belted around with a 7.15 ERA his past two starts, giving up seven homers and 15 hits in 11.1 innings, this was a massive improvement.
"I thought he was really good,'' Boone said. "You know he grinded pretty hard. Between the last start and this one, there are subtle adjustments you make that a lot of people probably over-reacted to.
"The reality is he's having an outstanding season. He's throwing the ball really well, and a great pitcher like him is going to be able to make some adjustments.''
Cole, who missed the entire 2025 season and the first 51 games this year, says he modified his mechanics to remake his delivery. Why, except for missing his location on a low fastball to Corbin Carroll in the second inning, resulting in a two-run homer, he was on-point with virtually all of his other pitches. He threw 90 pitches − 62 for strikes − without walking a batter.
"I mean, I don't think we did a perfect job tonight,'' Cole said. "I think we moved the needle in the right direction. I think there's some meat on the bone there. It's not easy, but it's necessary. It's the big leagues.''
Yep, just like no one is going to feel sorry for the Yankees with the loss of Judge. Not the Tampa Bay Rays, who are still in first place with a four-game lead. Not the Boston Red Sox, who the Yankees likely will face in the first round. Not a soul outside the Yankees organization.
"We have a lot of confidence in here,'' Cole said. "I mean, for the most part of the summer, we've been tested really, really hard, and responded − by and large − really well.
"We have a lot of perfectionists in here. We're always trying to be perfect, and always striving to be the best. But the reality is we've had a lot of obstacles that we've had to overcome, and we've played really well. So we're looking forward to more challenges to come.''
Yes, with or without Judge. The Yankees went 46-39 when he was out 100 days with a rib fracture, and they believe they're built for October. They know they have four top-quality starters and a deep bullpen that can dominate anyone.
"That's probably our biggest strength,'' Boone said. "Whoever we hand the ball to every day, we know is going to give us an opportunity to win a game.''
They proved that this night, with Judge merely watching from the bench, knowing he may have played his final game of the season.
"We're obviously bummed for Aaron, and Aaron's probably bummed too,'' Cole said, "but we've been in this position before this year. Unfortunately, it's our reality at this point.''
Follow Nightengale on X: @Bnightengale
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: No Aaron Judge, no problem? Yankees show they're still a force to be reckoned with

item.title: [New York Daily News] Yankees’ Gerrit Cole bounces back after getting pre-playoff vote of confidence
item.dc:creator: Gary Phillips
item.description: PHOENIX — With Gerrit Cole fresh off two rough outings, Aaron Boone quieted conversation over whether the longtime ace should get a postseason start, especially if the second-place Yankees find themselves in a best-of-three Wild Card series. Asked if Cole would be guaranteed a start in the Wild Card round, the likeliest scenario for the Yankees, the manager replied with a sly smile on Friday. “I would expect Gerrit Cole to start, yes,” Boone said before the righty started the Bombers’ 9-2, serie
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — With Gerrit Cole fresh off two rough outings, Aaron Boone quieted conversation over whether the longtime ace should get a postseason start, especially if the second-place Yankees find themselves in a best-of-three Wild Card series.
Asked if Cole would be guaranteed a start in the Wild Card round, the likeliest scenario for the Yankees, the manager replied with a sly smile on Friday.
“I would expect Gerrit Cole to start, yes,” Boone said before the righty started the Bombers’ 9-2, series-opening win over the Diamondbacks.
While the skipper was not completely definitive, Yankees pitching coach Matt Blake noted that Cole is lined up to pitch in the Wild Card round, which begins Sept. 29. As things stand, the Yankees would host the Red Sox, who have hit Cole well throughout his career.
Blake added that the Yankees have yet to formally discuss their postseason rotation plans, which also have to account for Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler, Max Fried and Carlos Rodón.
As a future Hall of Famer and the 2023 American League Cy Young, it would be shocking if Cole was not tabbed for a postseason start. However, the question was posed to Boone after Cole surrendered nine earned runs and seven homers over 16.2 innings in his previous two games against the Padres and Mets. Even prior to that, strikeouts and swing-and-miss had been hard to come by for Cole.
The 36-year-old, now 21 starts removed from Tommy John surgery, entered Friday with a 21.6 Whiff%, his lowest since 2016, and a 24.6 K%, his lowest since 2017. While he proceeded to strike out six D-Backs batters, he only induced six whiffs on 41 swings and 90 pitches.
Still, the evening represented a bounce-back start for Cole. After working to tighten up his delivery and improve his deception on the mound, the veteran completed six innings while also totaling four hits, two earned runs, zero walks and five hard-hit balls. The only runs Cole permitted came on a two-run, second-inning homer from Corbin Carroll, who smoked a 97.3-mph fastball that missed its spot.
Cole’s four-seamer had been a problem for him in his last two starts, yielding just six whiffs while being the target of 15 hard-hit balls.
While Cole was certainly better on Friday, his fastball and swing-and-miss woes are still something to keep an eye on with him scheduled to get one more regular season start. Blake said the latter can be attributed to “a host of things,” including Cole’s sequencing, command and the lack of deception that he worked on.
“I don’t think we did a perfect job tonight,” Cole said of his delivery. “I think we moved the needle in the right direction, but there’s still some meat on the bone there.”
Blake also noted that Cole hasn’t left the strike zone to get chase when given the opportunity in two-strike counts. Cole shared the same thought after his last start against the Mets.
One non-factor, according to Boone, Blake and Cole, is fatigue. All three have said that there is no reason to think Cole’s surgically repaired arm is tired, and he has said that he feels fine physically.
“Obviously, he’s getting up to the innings threshold we talked about in the beginning of the year, but he seems to be responding well,” Blake said. “The ball’s coming out with similar life, and the metrics are in line, so that doesn’t seem to be the case.”
With Friday’s game in the books, Cole has now logged 121.1 innings this season. With a 3.63 ERA, he’s put together a strong body of work after missing the entire 2025 season.
Boone, however, insisted Cole has had a “great” season before Friday’s win, and he took it a step further afterward.
“A lot of people probably overreacted to a couple of outings that, frankly, are inevitable in a long season. The reality is, he’s having an outstanding season,” Boone said. “He’s throwing the ball really well and a great pitcher like him is going to be able to make some adjustments when you have a couple where they get to you.”
While that’s an exaggeration by Cole’s lofty standards, one thing is certain with the playoffs nearing.
“He’s going to be a heavy factor for us,” Blake said.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] La Crisis De Aaron Judge, De Los Yankees, Se Agrava Mientras Boone Repite Ocho Veces La Misma Frase Enigmática
item.dc:creator: Inna Zeyger
item.description: PHOENIX — Los Yankees han demostrado cómo se puede ganar sin Aaron Judge. El viernes, en el Chase Field, Nueva York se puso por delante de los Arizona Diamondbacks con cinco carreras en la primera entrada y luego se llevó una cómoda victoria por 9-2. Con esta victoria, los Yankees suman ahora 89 victorias y 64 derrotas, reducen a cuatro partidos su desventaja respecto a Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana y mantienen la presión sobre los Rays de cara a la serie de cuatro partidos
item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Los Yankees han demostrado cómo se puede ganar sin Aaron Judge.
El viernes, en el Chase Field, Nueva York se puso por delante de los Arizona Diamondbacks con cinco carreras en la primera entrada y luego se llevó una cómoda victoria por 9-2. Con esta victoria, los Yankees suman ahora 89 victorias y 64 derrotas, reducen a cuatro partidos su desventaja respecto a Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana y mantienen la presión sobre los Rays de cara a la serie de cuatro partidos de la próxima semana en el Yankee Stadium.
Pero esa noche también traía consigo una cuestión mucho más grave, propia de octubre. Judge no estaba en la alineación, no se le pudo ver en el vestuario antes del partido y ya no se limitaba a aprovechar la última semana de la temporada regular solo para afinar su ritmo. Tras siete partidos desde su regreso tras una ausencia de 99 días por una fractura por estrés en la primera costilla derecha, el capitán de los Yankees volvió a convertirse en el centro de la incertidumbre del equipo de cara a la postemporada.
Ese momento es importante porque Judge apenas había empezado a recuperar su swing. Acabó con 4 de 23, un jonrón y 13 strikeouts tras volver el 8 de septiembre. Los Yankees lo habían ido incorporando poco a poco con partidos más cortos, un día como bateador designado y días de descanso, intentando equilibrar la urgencia de septiembre con la realidad de que se había perdido 84 partidos.
Los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero su camino más probable empieza con la Serie de Comodín de la Liga Americana el 29 de septiembre. Se suponía que la recta final de la temporada regular de Judge incluiría a Arizona, una serie directa de cuatro partidos contra Tampa Bay y la serie de cierre contra Baltimore. En cambio, los Yankees llegaron al fin de semana sin dar ninguna respuesta oficial sobre cuándo podría volver a jugar su mejor bateador.
El patrón de ocho palabras de Boone se convierte en la historia
Los Yankees confirmaron entonces la noticia sobre Aaron Judge que había generado tanta incertidumbre. El capitán fue incluido el sábado en la lista de lesionados de 10 días por una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha, con efecto retroactivo desde el jueves. La fecha más temprana en la que podría volver a jugar es el 27 de septiembre, pero Aaron Boone no dio ningún plazo ni grado de gravedad después de que una resonancia magnética confirmara la lesión.
Durante la rueda de prensa del viernes, Boone usó la frase «no lo sé» ocho veces mientras respondía a preguntas sobre la lesión, el tratamiento, el plazo de recuperación y su disponibilidad para la postemporada. Cuando le preguntaron directamente si los Yankees esperaban que Judge volviera en octubre, Boone dio la misma respuesta.
«No lo sé», dijo Boone.
Boone no quiso fijar una fecha concreta para la recuperación de Judge ni pronosticar si estará listo para cuando empiece la fase final.
«No tengo una fecha prevista para su vuelta», dijo Boone. «No voy a hacer predicciones. Obviamente, lo trataremos y ya veremos qué pasa».
El tratamiento no supuso una mejora suficiente
Judge empezó a notar una molestia mientras jugaba en el jardín derecho en la primera entrada del partido del miércoles en Minnesota. Siguió en el partido hasta que Heliot Ramos entró como bateador suplente en su lugar en la sexta entrada. Judge dijo después que intentó seguir jugando porque los partidos eran importantes.
«No me pareció una buena idea insistir demasiado en esto», dijo Judge.
El tratamiento del jueves no supuso una mejora suficiente, por lo que se decidieron hacer más pruebas. La resonancia magnética reveló la distensión. Judge seguirá con el tratamiento, y una inyección de plasma rico en plaquetas es una de las opciones una vez que los Yankees vuelvan a Nueva York.
Boone también dijo que no cuestionó que Judge se saltara una fase de rehabilitación en las ligas menores tras la lesión en las costillas. Los Yankees le habían limitado las entradas y le habían dado días de descanso.
«Estas cosas pasan tanto si hay una asignación de rehabilitación como si no. Hicimos todo lo que pudimos para intentar darle a él y a nosotros mismos la mejor oportunidad de que todo saliera bien», dijo Boone.
Un balance positivo sin Judge oculta el coste ofensivo
Los Yankees han aguantado sin Judge en la clasificación, pero hay que poner en contexto estos resultados. Nueva York tenía un balance de 41-25 cuando Judge era titular hasta el miércoles y de 47-39 cuando no lo era. La victoria del viernes dejó a los Yankees con un balance de 48-39 sin él, frente al 41-25 en los partidos en los que fue titular.
Desde el 2 de junio hasta el 7 de septiembre, los Yankees ocuparon el puesto 29 de las Grandes Ligas con un wRC+ de 90 y un promedio de bateo de 0,227, mientras que su OPS de 0,681 les situó en el puesto 27. El pitcheo ayudó a mantener la estabilidad de la temporada mientras la alineación sobrellevaba la larga ausencia de Judge.
Judge tiene un promedio de bateo de .241/.360/.511, con 18 jonrones y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos. El tres veces MVP de la Liga Americana también sufrió una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha en 2020, pero los Yankees no han dado a entender que la lesión actual sea igual de grave ni que el tiempo de recuperación vaya a ser el mismo.
Octubre sigue siendo una incógnita
Se espera que Max Schuemann vuelva de la Triple A este sábado. Los Yankees irán alternando sus opciones en los jardines mientras Judge recibe tratamiento, y él se perderá la serie de cuatro partidos contra los Rays.
Cody Bellinger dijo que la alineación no puede permitirse ponerse nerviosa como lo hizo durante la anterior ausencia de Judge. Los bateadores que quedan siguen teniendo las mismas expectativas.
«Vamos a tener que encontrar la manera», dijo Bellinger. «Creo que el talento que hay en este vestuario habla por sí solo, y estoy totalmente convencido de que tenemos suficiente talento aquí como para salir al campo, ganar y vencer a cualquiera».
Judge podría estar listo el 27 de septiembre, dos días antes de la Serie de Comodines, pero estar listo no significa estar preparado. Hasta que la pantorrilla responda y los Yankees establezcan un plan de recuperación, la respuesta que Boone repite una y otra vez sigue siendo la descripción más clara del estado de Judge para octubre: no lo saben.
¿Qué opinas? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Dos noches antes, la pelota se le había escapado por debajo del guante y había contribuido a que los Yankees cayeran derrotados en un partido de 13 entradas. El novato se lo tomó muy a pecho. El viernes, George Lombard Jr. respondió de la única forma en que puede hacerlo un jugador joven: con un bate lo suficientemente contundente como para ahogar ese recuerdo.
Conectó un sencillo de dos carreras en la primera entrada. Se llevó un jonrón en la sexta. Al final de la noche, sumaba dos hits y tres carreras impulsadas, y el campocorto que parecía desconcertado en Minnesota se mostraba ahora como una pieza clave del equipo.
La coincidencia fue casi cruel por su simetría. La misma tarde en que el equipo se preparaba para recibir el golpe más duro por una lesión en meses, su jugador titular menos consolidado cuajó su partido más sólido.
Lo que podría haber sido un golpe bajo se convirtió en toda una declaración de intenciones. Y esa declaración no tuvo casi nada que ver con el hombre por el que todos estaban preocupados.
Los Yankees arrollaron a los Diamondbacks por 9-2 en el Chase Field el viernes por la noche, unas horas después de enterarse de que Aaron Judge volvería a la lista de lesionados por una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha que podría poner fin a su temporada regular. Nueva York mejoró su balance a 89-64, sumó su undécima victoria en 15 partidos y se colocó a cuatro partidos de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, después de que los Rays perdieran 4-2 ante Boston. Los Yankees también mantuvieron una ventaja de 5 partidos y medio sobre los Red Sox por el primer puesto de comodín de la Liga Americana.
Una primera entrada de cinco carreras en la que no hizo falta ninguna superestrella
El modelo a seguir para una vida sin Judge quedó claro enseguida. Los Yankees enviaron a 10 bateadores al plato contra el zurdo de Arizona, Eduardo Rodríguez, y anotaron cinco veces antes de que se produjera el segundo out.
Los cinco primeros bateadores llegaron a base. Paul Goldschmidt consiguió una base por bolas , Cody Bellinger conectó un sencillo y, tras otra base por bolas, Ben Rice consiguió una base por bolas con las bases llenas, lo que permitió anotar una carrera. Amed Rosario conectó un sencillo de un toque que impulsó una carrera, un pase fallido permitió que Heliot Ramos anotara y Lombard conectó un sencillo de dos carreras por el centro para poner el 5-0 en el marcador.
No fue un solo golpe fulminante. Fueron nueve bateadores que obligaron a un ex All-Star a lanzar 45 veces en la primera entrada. Esa paciencia es el tipo de ataque que más necesitarán los Yankees en octubre, cuando la ausencia de Judge convierta cada remontada en un esfuerzo colectivo.
Cole se recompone y luego hace historia
La ventaja le permitió a Gerrit Cole respirar tranquilo. El lanzador diestro había encajado siete jonrones en sus dos últimas salidas, y se habían intensificado los rumores sobre si estaría listo para octubre. Con esta actuación, acalló gran parte de esos rumores.
Cole encajó un jonrón de dos carreras de Corbin Carroll en la segunda entrada, de nuevo con una bola rápida que se quedó en el plato, pero nada más. Lanzó seis entradas, cedió dos carreras con cuatro hits, no concedió ninguna base por bolas y ponchó a seis con 90 lanzamientos. Boone había dicho antes del partido que Cole sería el abridor en la serie de comodín de todas formas.
Cole se tomó esta salida como un paso adelante, no como una solución definitiva. Explicó que había dedicado el tiempo entre sus salidas a afinar su lanzamiento para mejorar su capacidad de engaño.
«No creo que lo hayamos hecho perfecto esta noche, pero sí que hemos dado un paso en la dirección correcta», dijo Cole. «Creo que todavía nos queda mucho por hacer. No es fácil, pero es necesario. Así son las grandes ligas».
Esta victoria fue la número 162 de la carrera de Cole, lo que le permitió superar a Mike Moore como el lanzador con más victorias de todos los tiempos entre los elegidos en primera posición en el draft de la MLB, un hito discreto en una noche llena de otros titulares.
Un error defensivo que se corrigió al instante
Esta es la jugada que da forma a la noche, y en la que pocos se fijarán. El error de Lombard dos días antes en Minnesota había formado parte de una secuencia decisiva que le costó a los Yankees un partido que podían haber ganado. El viernes se presentó algo que el deporte rara vez concede tan rápido: una segunda oportunidad sin condiciones.
Su jonrón en la sexta entrada sacó a Rodríguez del partido y amplió la ventaja a 7-2. Para un novato que se vio obligado a ocupar el puesto de campocorto en la recta final, su reacción importó más que las carreras. Cuando le preguntaron por la noche, Lombard lo dejó claro.
«Fue genial desde el principio, todos hicimos buenos turnos al bate», dijo Lombard. «Obviamente, había un buen lanzador en el montículo. Le hicimos trabajar».
Esta actuación llega justo cuando los Yankees están valorando los roles para la postemporada en el cuadro, donde la solidez de un novato ahora tiene un peso real de cara a octubre.
Rice se acerca a los 40 mientras Judge se queda en el banquillo
Rice le dio a los Yankees otro pilar. Su jonrón en la tercera entrada contra Rodríguez recorrió 390 pies y fue el número 39 de la temporada, una cifra que, según el entrenador Aaron Boone, ya había predicho en los entrenamientos de primavera. Rice terminó con ese jonrón y un triple, y suma cinco jonrones en sus últimos 22 partidos.
El ambiente en torno a ese swing era sombrío. Judge había impulsado tantas primeras entradas a lo largo de los años, y ahora los Yankees tienen que volver a luchar por llegar a octubre sin él. Rice se refirió a lo difícil que resulta este momento.
«Es un duro golpe para nosotros», dijo Rice. «Llevábamos mucho tiempo echándole de menos, así que esto nos cuesta especialmente aceptarlo. Pero no nos queda más remedio que seguir jugando a tope y seguir haciendo lo nuestro».
Los Yankees creen que el pitcheo les llevará a la victoria pase lo que pase. Cam Schlittler, el probable ganador del Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, está previsto que sea el abridor en un posible primer partido de la ronda de comodines, con Max Fried y Carlos Rodón como relevos.
Nueva York y Arizona vuelven a enfrentarse este sábado, con Schlittler listo para medirse a Brandon Pfaadt. La inminente serie de cuatro partidos contra los Rays en el Yankee Stadium, que empieza el martes con una doble jornada, podría decidir el título de la división. Por una noche, un novato algo desconcertado y un as que se mantuvo firme hicieron que los Yankees parecieran listos.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees news: Aaron Boone drops huge Cam Schlittler Cy Young prediction appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
Aaron Boone was asked a simple question about Cam Schlittler's impact on the Yankees rotation. His answer skipped straight past the premise.
"He's going to win the Cy Young," Boone said during his pregame press conference. "You got an ace at the top that's pitched like that. That's a good place to start. He's been dominant."
"Well, he's gonna win the Cy Young!"
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Aaron Boone on what Cam Schlittler has meant to the Yankees' rotation this season. pic.twitter.com/VzFIYOzdb4
— YES Network (@YESNetwork) September 18, 2026
The manager is not out on a limb. Through 31 starts and 184 2/3 innings this season, Schlittler owns a 1.95 ERA and a 0.90 WHIP, leading the American League in ERA, innings and WHIP while sitting near the top in strikeouts. He has already set a franchise record with 20 starts of one run or fewer, and he became the fourth-youngest Yankee to reach 200 strikeouts in a season. Dylan Cease is the only serious challenger, and his edge is limited to total strikeouts.
Boone traced the rise back further than this year. "I think he's just continued to get better year in and year out," he said. "This is largely in line with who we saw down the stretch when he got called up last year. Obviously had about as dominant a postseason outing as you could against the Red Sox and it's carried that right into this year."
That October showing came in Schlittler's first playoff run, where he posted a 1.26 ERA across 14 1/3 innings after a 2.96 ERA over 73 regular-season frames as a rookie. A seventh-round pick out of Northeastern in 2022, he has climbed faster than anyone in the organization projected.
Boone credited the makeup as much as the arm. "He's got great stuff. Obviously, he's a tremendous competitor," he said. "He's got a real good way about him, ability to make adjustments start to start, not be overwhelmed by a result start to start, and he's put it all together for a full season now at this level."
Schlittler would be New York's second Cy Young winner in four years after Gerrit Cole in 2023, and his 2026 numbers have outpaced Cole's award-winning campaign. The Yankees have already clinched a playoff berth.
Related: Yankees' Aaron Judge landing on IL comes with Game 162 catch
Related: Has Yankees' Cam Schlittler been as good as Jacob Misiorowski this season?

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Aaron Judge is on the injured list again, but the Yankees could get two key pieces back off of it by next week.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. should be activated on the upcoming homestand that begins Tuesday, Aaron Boone said Friday, after the second baseman landed on the IL last week with a right thumb sprain.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
Friday marked his fourth day of hitting in a row after being shut down from baseball activities for about a week, while he has also been throwing the last couple of days.
“He’s getting very close,” Boone said before the Yankees’ 9-2 win over the Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
Trent Grisham, meanwhile, is “pretty far into his running progression” from a right hamstring strain and “doing well,” Boone said, putting him in position to be in play at the end of the regular season.
Before Judge’s calf strain, it was questionable whether there would be a lane for Grisham to get playing time if and when he returned.
But now it is possible he could return to center field at least against righties, bumping Spencer Jones to right field.
As for Ryan Weathers, the other Yankee trying to make it back in time for the playoffs (from a left forearm flexor strain), Boone acknowledged the lefty is “unlikely to get into a game before the end of the season.”
Weathers is set to throw a second bullpen session on Saturday, after which he could advance to facing hitters in live batting practice.
Whether that will give him enough time to show he should be part of the bullpen for the first round of the playoffs remains to be seen.
“We’ll see what our needs are and how he looks and if we feel like he’s ready to come in and be a contributor,” Boone said.
Anthony Volpe, who was back at second base, hit .348 with a .965 OPS and four steals in his first seven games since being called back up from Triple-A as an injury replacement for Chisholm.
He was 0-for-4 in Friday night’s win.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX - Gerrit Cole nunca había permitido siete jonrones en un lapso de dos aperturas antes de sus salidas más recientes y, con los playoffs a la vuelta de la esquina, existía la preocupación de que el lanzador derecho de los Yankees hubiera sufrido un bajón de rendimiento.
La mayor parte de esa inquietud provenía de fuera del vestuario. El manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone, afirmó el viernes que se esperaba que Cole abriera un partido si su equipo llegaba a la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Americana, y el veterano cumplió su promesa de solucionar el problema de los cuadrangulares y lanzó bien en la victoria por 9-2 sobre los Diamondbacks en el Chase Field el viernes por la noche.
Los Yankees (89-64) ganaron por 11ma vez en 15 partidos, colocándose a cuatro juegos de los Rays en la División Este de la Liga Americana después de que Tampa Bay perdiera ante Boston más temprano esa misma noche.
Horas después de que Cody Bellinger dijera que los Yankees tendrían que "apoyarse mutuamente" para superar la ausencia de Aaron Judge —quien, tras ganar tres veces el premio al Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana, podría perderse el resto de la temporada regular debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha—, los "Bombarderos" respaldaron a Cole con una primera entrada de cinco carreras.
Cada uno de los primeros cinco bateadores se embasó y anotó ante el venzolano Eduardo Rodríguez. Ben Rice negoció una base por bolas con las bases llenas, el dominicano Amed Rosario conectó un sencillo productor y George Lombard Jr. disparó un sencillo de dos carreras; esto fue parte de una noche de tres carreras impulsadas para el novato, quien también conectó un jonrón en la sexta entrada que provocó la salida de Rodríguez del juego.
Rice también conectó su 39no jonrón —líder del equipo— para apoyar a Cole, quien había permitido jonrones al primer bateador en sus dos aperturas anteriores. Tras dedicar tiempo a ajustar su mecánica de lanzamiento y corregir posibles problemas de revelación de pitcheos desde su última salida contra los Mets, Cole retiró a los bateadores de Arizona en orden durante una primera entrada de 12 lanzamientos.
Corbin Carroll conectó un jonrón de dos carreras ante Cole en la segunda entrada, pero eso fue todo lo que lograron los D-backs. Con un total de 90 lanzamientos (62 strikes), Cole permitió cuatro imparables, no otorgó bases por bolas y ponchó a seis bateadores.

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] Yankees ride five-run first to series-opening romp of Diamondbacks
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: The two starting pitchers entered this game trending in opposite directions. Gerrit Cole had just allowed the most home runs (seven) in a two-start span in his career, while Eduardo Rodriguez is in the midst of a career year with a 2.62 ERA. item.content:encoded:
The two starting pitchers entered this game trending in opposite directions. Gerrit Cole had just allowed the most home runs (seven) in a two-start span in his career, while Eduardo Rodriguez is in the midst of a career year with a 2.62 ERA. One of those trends remained — Cole giving up another home run on a fastball — but fortunately the other trend was momentarily halted, the Yankees scoring five in the first off E-Rod to give themselves enough of a cushion to weather Cole’s continued home run woes.
Cole settled down after the Carroll dinger to give the Yankees six innings, by which time the offense all but put this game out of reach. They kept the pressure on, scoring a further four runs including solo home runs by Ben Rice and George Lombard Jr., to cruise to a series-opening victory in the desert, 9-2.
Rodriguez came into this game with an ERA above six in the first inning and an ERA right around two for the subsequent innings combined. That made it imperative that the Yankees find a way to do damage before the home team had a chance to come to bat, especially with the rate Cole is giving up the long ball. They did just that with a clear disciplined approach not to expand the zone against E-Rod’s curveball.
Paul Goldschmidt drew a leadoff walk, Cody Bellinger followed with a single, and Heliot Ramos also walked to load the bases with no outs. Rice drew the Yankees’ third walk in the first four batters to plate Goldschmidt and open the scoring, Goldy, Ramos, and Rice all working full counts before taking the free pass. Amed Rosario then fought off a cutter that handcuffed him up and in, muscling it to the opposite field perfectly between center and left fielder to plate Bellinger as the runners went station to station. A wild pitch allowed Ramos to score and Rice and Rosario to move up to second and third. This set up a two-run ground ball single from Lombard that just got by Geraldo Perdomo’s diving attempt to atone for his defensive misplay in the 13th that allowed the Twins to walk off the Yankees on Wednesday.
Rodriguez struck out Volpe to end the inning giving him three strikeouts in the frame, but the damage was done. The 45 pitches he threw were the most he’s thrown in the first inning in his career. 33 of those pitches fell out of the zone, but only eight induced a chase.
It’s a good thing they hung such a crooked number, because Cole immediately gave two of those runs back. He gave up a leadoff single to Perdomo before yanking an 0-1 four-seamer right into Corbin Carroll’s nitro zone, the three-time All-Star obliterating it to right for a two-run bomb to reduce the Yankees’ lead, 5-2. Rice made sure to immediately tilt the momentum back in his team’s favor. After falling behind 0-2, he stayed back on an elevated heater from E-Rod riding it out the other way and over the fence in left-center for a leadoff bomb, his 39th of the year, to give Cole some more of his cushion back, 6-2.
Cole settled down to work a scoreless third and fourth, helped in part by a sharp uptick in slider usage at the expense of some four-seamers as well as an impressive sliding catch in left-center by Spencer Jones in the third. He finally began dialing the fastball command to the corners in the fifth, striking out Tim Tawa and Lars Nootbaar on four-seamers to end the frame after Jesús Sánchez singled with one out. This allowed Lombard to restore the Yankees’ five run lead in the sixth, the rookie punishing a hanging curveball from E-Rod by lining the solo shot down the line it left and into the bullpen for his fourth of the year and third RBI on the night.
The four-seamer was the prime culprit for Cole in his previous two starts with a 68.2-percent hard-hit rate and just six whiffs, and that remained the case tonight. However, I believe it is Cole’s rustiness with his secondaries that is leading his four-seamer to get barreled. The fastball still has plenty of velocity — at 97 mph it’s a full tick above last season. I will grant that he has missed location in the zone on numerous occasions which hasn’t done him any favors.
However, after his last start, Cole identified a lack of chase and whiff against his secondaries as the reason his fastball is getting crushed. Hitters being able to lay off those chase pitches forces Cole to overuse the fastball in counts that favor the softer stuff, which in essence gives them the opportunity to hunt the heater when they should be defending against the breaker. When you can hunt a fastball in any count, chances are you are going to do damage when Cole misses his spot in the zone, the high velocity not much of a weapon when hitters’ bats are preemptively sped up.
Indeed, once he started commanding his slider and knuckle curve to the shadow of the zone in the middle innings, the hard contact against the fastball dried up. Having pitched a strong fifth and sixth and with his pitch count at 90, Boone saw no reason to overextend Cole and ended his night after six with his best innings freshest in mind. He finished night having pitched six innings, allowing two runs on four hits with no walks and six strikeouts.
Despite possessing one of the stingiest bullpens in baseball, the Diamondbacks decided that a five-run deficit in the seventh was too steep to justify using their high leverage arms. So, Zac Gallen made his first career relief appearance, the former All-Star in the midst of am injury-plagued, below-replacement-level campaign. He allowed a leadoff single to Goldschmidt and walked Ramos and Rice — again, both in full counts — to load the bases with one out. Aaron Boone sent out Ryan McMahon to pinch-hit for Rosario, and he hit a sharp grounder to first that Pavin Smith gloved but airmailed the underhand toss to Gallen covering first as all the runners were safe and a run scored on the error. Spencer Jones then appeared to ground into the inning-ending double play, but his hustle out of the box and down the line just beat the throw to pick up an RBI and make it 9-2.
Ryan Yarbrough pitched 1.1 innings in relief of Cole and worked himself into and out of trouble in the seventh. Arizona put runners on second and third as Nolan Arenado singled and Carroll doubled with one out. However, Yarbrough struck out Jose Fernandez and Tawa to strand the pair in scoring position. Rice smoked his fourth triple of the year in the ninth but was stranded at third by a McMahon strikeout. Michael Fulmer and Luis Gil recorded the final five outs of the game without allowing a baserunner to seal the win, 9-2. With the Rays having lost to the Red Sox earlier in the evening, the Yankees’ deficit is back to four games in the division, making that looming four-game set against Tampa in the Bronx even more high stakes.
Cam Schlittler looks to cement his AL Cy Young case tomorrow after Dylan Cease suffered his shortest start of the season on Friday. The Yankees ace will face off against Brandon Pfaadt with a slightly more reasonable game start time. First pitch is scheduled for 8:10 pm ET with the broadcast remaining on YES.
Yankees rout the D-Backs, 9-2, who's your Player of the Game?
Gerrit Cole pitched 6 innings of 2-run ball. George Lombard Jr. hit a two-run single and a solo homer. Ben Rice raked with a solo homer, triple, and two walks.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Gerrit Cole had never surrendered seven home runs over a two-start span before his most recent outings, and with the playoffs around the corner, there was concern that the Yankees’ right-hander might have hit a wall.
Most of that came from outside the clubhouse. Yankees manager Aaron Boone affirmed Friday that Cole should expect to draw a start if his team lands in the American League Wild Card Series, and the veteran made good on his promise to fix the long-ball issue, pitching well in a 9-2 victory over the Diamondbacks at Chase Field on Friday night.
Hours after Cody Bellinger said the Yankees would have to “lean on each other” to overcome Aaron Judge’s absence, with the three-time AL MVP potentially set to miss the rest of the regular season with a right calf strain, the Bombers supported Cole with a five-run first inning.
Each of the first five batters reached base and scored against Eduardo Rodriguez. Ben Rice worked a bases-loaded walk, Amed Rosario lifted a run-scoring single and George Lombard Jr. stroked a two-run single -- part of a three-RBI night for the rookie, who launched a sixth-inning homer that chased Rodriguez.
Rice also slugged his team-leading 39th home run to support Cole, who had served up leadoff homers in his previous two starts. Having spent time focusing on his delivery and potential pitch-tipping issues since his last outing against the Mets, Cole set Arizona down in order during a 12-pitch first inning.
Corbin Carroll cracked a two-run homer in the second inning off Cole, but that was all the D-backs managed. Throwing 90 pitches (62 for strikes), Cole scattered four hits, walking none and striking out six.

item.content:encoded:
On Friday night, the New York Yankees are playing the first game of their series with the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
They are coming off a series where they won two out of three games over the Minnesota Twins at Target Field.
New York Yankees Announced Chisholm Jr. Update
The Yankees continue to play without one of their best players, as Jazz Chisholm Jr. has been out since September 8 with an injury.
Ahead of Friday’s game, manager Aaron Boone shared the latest on the two-time MLB All-Star.
Bryan Hoch of MLB.com wrote: “Jazz Chisholm Jr. is “doing well” and should be activated on this homestand, Aaron Boone said.”
Before getting hurt, Chisholm Jr. had been batting .232 with 107 hits, 19 home runs, 55 RBIs, 68 runs and 40 stolen bases in 134 games.
MLB.com also wrote (on September 18): “Went on the IL on Sept. 10 and will have no baseball activities for 7-10 days. “Doing well,” Aaron Boone said Sept. 18, Chisholm’s fourth consecutive day of hitting. He has also been throwing.”
Looking At Chisholm Jr.
Chisholm Jr. is in the middle of his third season playing for the Yankees.
Prior to New York, he had spent the first 4.5 seasons of his career on the Miami Marlins.
In 2024, Chisholm Jr. helped the Yankees reach the World Series.
This winter, Chisholm Jr. will be among the most intriguing free agents to hit the market.
He will turn 29 in February.
Yankees On Friday
The Yankees are the second-place team in the American League East.
They have gone 88-64 in 152 games.
Following three games in Arizona, the Yankees will host the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday.

item.title: [Larry Brown Sports] Aaron Boone's comments on Aaron Judge injury will have Yankees fans concerned
item.dc:creator: Renzo Pocholo Salao

With less than two weeks until the playoffs begin, reporters asked Boone Friday whether Judge would be back in the lineup in time for the posts
item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone does not sound confident about Aaron Judge’s odds of returning this season.
Judge left in the middle of the Yankees’ Wednesday tilt against the Minnesota Twins with an injury the team initially labeled as right leg soreness. Two days later, the Yankees announced that they were placing Judge on the 10-day injured list.
With less than two weeks until the playoffs begin, reporters asked Boone Friday whether Judge would be back in the lineup in time for the postseason. The Yankees skipper did not sound convinced.
“I don’t know,” Boone responded, via USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. “I don’t have a timeline on it. I can’t predict anything. … I mean, we have no idea, we’re in the early stages. We’ll just obviously treat it and see what transpires.”
Boone spoke further about the Yankees learning to play without Judge, who has spent more than half the season on the mend.
“The reality is that we’ve had to play a lot of the season this year without him,’’ Boone said. “There’s no replacing a player as great as Aaron Judge, but you know we have high expectations that don’t change now. We have a lot of confidence in the people we run out there every day. We’re going to match up day in and day out, and the goal doesn’t change.”
The Yankees lost Judge for 84 games this season after he sustained a rib injury in April. He tried to play through the issue and had an unproductive May until the team decided to shut him down.
New York maintained a winning pace during that span, going 45-39 in the 84 games without its captain. But winning gets a lot harder once the lights get brighter in the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Cam Schlittler sported a significant bruise on his right hamstring as he moved through the visiting clubhouse at Chase Field on Friday afternoon. It was a souvenir from his most recent start, which ended after the Mets’ Bo Bichette connected on a 111.5 mph comebacker.
That ball dented flesh, but Schlittler’s season has been so charmed, even the hard-hit balls are turning into outs. Bichette’s knock ricocheted to catcher Austin Wells, who tossed on to first base, sealing Schlittler’s six scoreless innings that day.
“It’s fun to watch. It’s fun to play behind,” Cody Bellinger said. “Even in the middle of the game, I was like, ‘This is unbelievable.’ You don’t really get that much.”
And while the league has had ample opportunity to take in Schlittler’s dominance, what impresses most from a distance of 60 feet and six inches?
“Probably the composure on the mound,” Wells said. “I think that’s the most impressive, besides obviously the numbers across the board. It’s just the way he handles every inning, every pitch. He expects the best every time he throws the ball. So it’s super impressive.”
That’s good news for the Yankees, who appear to be lining up Schlittler to start a potential Game 1 of the American League Wild Card Series against the Red Sox.
“You’ve got an ace at the top that’s pitched like that, that’s a good place to start,” manager Aaron Boone said. “He’s been dominant. I think he’s just continued to get better, year in and year out.”
“The expectation is to make the playoffs, and the expectation is to win a championship,” Schlittler said. “We’re in a good spot if we keep playing the way we’re playing.”
With Schlittler deep into his longest season yet, Wells believes his batterymate is finding new layers of sharpness.
“I think we’ve seen games where he doesn’t have the best command, but he still gets through it,” Wells said. “There’s another layer to that command piece, that makes it effectively a little bit wild sometimes. I think when he continues to improve that, he’s just going to continue to get better.”
Schlittler’s 1.95 ERA is the second-lowest by a Yankee through 31 starts since Ron Guidry’s 1.71 ERA in 1978, when “Louisiana Lightning” won the Cy Young and finished second in the MVP race to Jim Rice of the Red Sox.
It was the 21st time Schlittler has allowed one run or fewer. That’s a franchise record, and over the last 110 years, only three pitchers age 25 or younger have had as many: Blake Snell (2018), Dean Chance (1964) and Babe Ruth (1916).
Yet Boone said he’s not surprised by Schlittler’s performance, saying it has been largely in line with what the Yankees saw after his late-season callup in 2025.
“He had about as dominant a postseason outing as you could against the Red Sox, and he has carried that right into this year,” Boone said. “He’s got great stuff, he’s a tremendous competitor and he has a real good way about him -- an ability to make adjustments start to start, not be overwhelmed by a result start to start, and he’s put it all together for a full season now at this level.”

item.title: [UNANIMO Deportes] ¡Aaron Judge vuelve a la lista de lesionados de los Yankees! - UNANIMO Deportes
item.dc:creator: Jocelyn Blasco
item.description: Los Yankees de Nueva York volverán a jugar sin su capitán en un momento clave de la temporada. Aaron Judge será colocado nuevamente en la lista de lesionados de 10 días, esta vez debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha, informó el equipo este viernes. La decisión llega apenas unos días después de que el tres veces MVP de la Liga Americana regresara de una lesión que lo mantuvo fuera durante gran parte de la campaña. - LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Dodgers ya son campeones de la División Oeste!
item.content:encoded:
Los Yankees de Nueva York volverán a jugar sin su capitán en un momento clave de la temporada. Aaron Judge será colocado nuevamente en la lista de lesionados de 10 días, esta vez debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha, informó el equipo este viernes. La decisión llega apenas unos días después de que el tres veces MVP de la Liga Americana regresara de una lesión que lo mantuvo fuera durante gran parte de la campaña.
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Dodgers ya son campeones de la División Oeste!
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¿Cómo cambia el último comodín de la Nacional en Padres vs. Marlins?
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
Judge había vuelto al terreno el 8 de septiembre, después de pasar alrededor de 100 días fuera por una fractura por estrés en la primera costilla derecha. El jardinero había evitado una asignación de rehabilitación en las Ligas Menores y regresó directamente al lineup de Nueva York para enfrentar a los Rockies de Colorado.
Sin embargo, su regreso duró poco. El miércoles 16 de septiembre, durante el encuentro contra los Twins de Minnesota, Judge fue retirado en la sexta entrada y sustituido por un bateador emergente. Después del partido explicó que había sentido rigidez en la parte baja de la pierna derecha desde la primera entrada y que, después de hablarlo con el equipo, consideró que lo mejor era abandonar el encuentro para evitar que la molestia se agravara.
La nueva lesión representa otro golpe para un jugador que apenas estaba retomando ritmo competitivo. Desde su regreso, Judge disputó seis encuentros y registró 4 imparables en 23 turnos (.174), un cuadrangular y varios ponches. En el balance de la temporada, suma .241 de promedio, .360 de porcentaje de embasado, .511 de slugging, 18 jonrones y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos.
El momento de la lesión también es particularmente relevante para los Yankees. Nueva York llegó a la jornada del viernes cinco juegos por detrás de los Rays de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, por lo que la ausencia de Judge se producirá durante una parte importante de la pelea por la posición en la tabla. El equipo, además, tendrá que afrontar una serie de cuatro encuentros contra Tampa Bay la próxima semana.
Ver esta publicación en Instagram
La buena noticia, al menos sobre el papel, es que la colocación en la lista de lesionados puede hacerse de manera retroactiva al jueves 17 de septiembre. Esto significa que la fecha más temprana para que Judge vuelva sería el 27 de septiembre, precisamente el último partido de la temporada regular, cuando los Yankees enfrenten a los Orioles de Baltimore.
El problema es que todavía no existe certeza sobre su regreso. Aaron Boone no ha establecido un calendario concreto para la recuperación de su capitán y tampoco aseguró que Judge pueda estar disponible para la postemporada. El Wild Card de la Liga Americana está programado para comenzar el 29 de septiembre, apenas dos días después del último encuentro de temporada regular.
Judge había sido una pieza fundamental para Nueva York antes de su primera lesión. La fractura de la costilla derecha lo llevó a la lista de lesionados en junio, después de que el jugador intentara competir durante varias semanas con molestias. Finalmente, los estudios determinaron que se trataba de una fractura por estrés, lo que provocó que se perdiera más de tres meses de actividad.
Ahora los Yankees tendrán que afrontar nuevamente el cierre de la temporada sin su principal figura ofensiva. El equipo deberá esperar la evolución de la pantorrilla derecha de Judge mientras continúa la lucha por definir su posición rumbo a octubre. Por ahora, el 27 de septiembre aparece como su posible fecha más temprana de regreso, pero su participación en la postemporada permanece en duda.

item.title: [Yardbarker] New York Yankees Make Spencer Jones Announcement
item.dc:creator: Simeon Kotto
item.description: The New York Yankees open a series in Arizona on Friday night looking to rebound from a one-run loss and find more consistent production from a young outfielder who has shown both power and growing pains. item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees open a series in Arizona on Friday night looking to rebound from a one-run loss and find more consistent production from a young outfielder who has shown both power and growing pains.
After falling 5-4 to the Minnesota Twins on Wednesday, the club posted its lineup for the first game against the Diamondbacks, and the most notable tweak involved Spencer Jones, via FantasyPros.
Jones had occupied the fifth spot in the order against Minnesota and finished without a hit while striking out five times. That performance prompted manager Aaron Boone to slide the 25-year-old down one place, into the sixth hole, for Friday’s contest.
The rest of the order features Paul Goldschmidt at first, Cody Bellinger in left, Heliot Ramos in right, Ben Rice as the designated hitter, Amed Rosario at third, George Lombard at short, Austin Wells behind the plate and Anthony Volpe at second. Jones will patrol center field.
The adjustment is modest on paper, yet it reflects the reality of a rookie season that has mixed encouraging numbers with stretches of swing-and-miss. Jones is hitting .252 with 59 hits, 10 home runs, 37 RBIs, 32 runs and nine stolen bases across 79 games.
Those totals represent real production for a player who made his major-league debut earlier this year after being selected in the first round of the 2022 draft out of Vanderbilt.
At 6-foot-7, 240 pounds, he possesses the kind of raw power that can change a game in a single swing, something he demonstrated with a three-run homer against the Twins just a few days earlier.
Still, five strikeouts in one night is the kind of night that forces a lineup shuffle. Boone has moved Jones around the order several times this season as the Yankees try to maximize his strengths while limiting damage against certain pitching looks.
The Diamondbacks series offers another chance to see whether a slightly lower spot in the batting order helps him settle in and put the ball in play more often.
New York arrives in Phoenix needing wins as the calendar moves deeper into September. A tight loss in Minnesota left little margin, and every at-bat from a developing bat like Jones carries extra weight.
The organization drafted him for his combination of size, athleticism and power; the challenge now is translating that package into more consistent contact at the highest level.
Friday’s lineup is a small tactical step in that process rather than a dramatic demotion.
Whether Jones responds with extra-base hits or continues to chase pitches remains to be seen. What is clear is that the Yankees still view him as part of their present and future outfield mix.
A drop from fifth to sixth is not a verdict on his season. It is simply the latest attempt to put a young player in a position where his next good swing can matter.

item.title: [CBS Sports] Yankees place Aaron Judge back on IL, making star slugger's status uncertain ahead of playoffs
item.dc:creator: Matt Snyder

item.content:encoded:
Yankees superstar Aaron Judge will be placed on the 10-day injured list on Saturday, the Yankees announced Friday evening prior to their game in Arizona. This comes two days after Judge exited in the middle of a game due to a right calf strain. Judge missed more than three months earlier this season with a wrist issue and played just seven games before landing back on the injured list.
There are only 10 days left in the season, but the Yankees can backdate the transaction, which would make the three-time MVP eligible to return from the injured list on the final day of the regular season, Sept. 27, though his body would need to cooperate. The Wild Card Series, which the Yankees will play in unless they can track down the Rays in the AL East, will begin on Tuesday, Sept. 29.
We can't be sure that the level of severity is similar, but for what it's worth, Judge had a strained calf in 2020 and missed roughly three weeks. A similar timeline this year, would see Judge return in the middle of the ALDS (if the Yankees reach the round).
As for when the Yankees expect him back? They don't know.
"I don't know," manager Aaron Boone told reporters on Friday. "I'm not going to predict anything."
Judge this season has 66 games played, hitting .241/.360/.511 (140 OPS+) with 18 homers, 41 RBI and 1.9 WAR. Judge homered against the Twins on Monday, but he was hitting just .174/.208/.304 in 24 plate appearances since returning from the wrist injury.
He has dealt with injuries in the past, but this season marks his lowest games played in a non-COVID season since he was called up late in the season as a rookie.
The Yankees have already clinched a playoff berth. They have an outside shot at winning the AL East and the top seed in the AL. They trail the Rays by five games, but there's a four-game series in Yankee Stadium next week. Judge will be sidelined for the entire series.
Of course, the Yankees without Judge are a different team. They are 41-25 when he starts and 47-39 when he doesn't. He's one of the most important players to a team in all of baseball.
The Yankees have a three-game stop in Arizona before finishing at home with a four-game series against the Rays and a three-game series against the Orioles.
